en: Unvarying; all the same.
Consistent; conforming to one standard.
A distinctive outfit that serves to identify members of a group, company, prison inmates, etc.
A uniformed police officer (as opposed to a detective).
To clothe in a uniform.

uniform.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ís?
Proto-Indo-European *h₁óynos
Proto-Italic *oinos
Old Latin oinos
Latin ūnus
Latin ūni-
Ancient Greek μορφή (morphḗ)der.?
Latin fōrma
Latin -fōrmis
Latin uniformis
Middle French uniformebor.
English uniform
Borrowed from Middle French uniforme, from Latin uniformis.

ex.en: Team members are provided with equipment and uniforms.
ex.ja: チームのメンバーは道具とユニフォームを提供されます。

ex.en: The new houses are of a uniform height.
ex.ja: それらの新築の家はみな同じ高さである。

ex.en: The school should do away with the uniform.
ex.ja: その学校は、制服を廃止すべきだ。

note.ja: uni（1つ）+ form（形）。1つの形の →「制服・一様な」。

en: undomesticated animals, especially mammals, birds, and fish, which live in the wild.
Living undomesticated organisms of all kinds.

wildlife.ety:
Etymology tree
English wild
Proto-Indo-European *leyp-der.
Proto-Germanic *lībanąder.
Proto-Germanic *lībą
Proto-West Germanic *līb
Old English līf
Middle English lyf
English life
English wildlife
From wild + life.

ex.en: The organization plays a principal role in wildlife conservation.
ex.ja: その団体は野生動物の保護において、最も重要な役割を果たしている。

ex.en: The area is notable for its scenery and wildlife.
ex.ja: その地域は風景と野生動物で注目に値する。

note.ja: wild（野生の）+ life（生命）。「野生生物」。

en: Made of wood.
As if made of wood; moving awkwardly, or speaking with dull lack of emotion.

wooden.ety:
PIE word
 *dwóh₁
From wood + -en. Dates from 1530s, gradually replaced treen (“made from a tree”), from Middle English treen, from Old English triewen.

ex.en: I'd rather live in a wooden house.
ex.ja: どちらかといえば木造住宅に住みたい。

ex.en: An old wooden box served as table.
ex.ja: 古い木箱がテーブルの役目をした。

ex.en: A wooden building can easily catch fire.
ex.ja: 木造家屋は簡単に燃える。

note.ja: wood（木）+ -en（〜でできた）。「木製の」→「ぎこちない」。golden と同じ作り。

en: Characterized by aggression; highly combative; prone to behave in a way that involves attacking (especially if unjustly) or arguing.
Tends to attack the player while unprovoked.
One who is aggressive.
A (Black) woman who presents as masculine; a butch.

aggressive.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂éd
Proto-Italic *ad
Proto-Italic *ad-
Latin ad-
Proto-Indo-European *gʰredʰ-der.
Latin gradior
Latin aggredior
Latin aggressuslbor.
English aggress
Proto-Indo-European *-wós
Proto-Indo-European *-iHwósder.
Latin -īvus
Old French -ifbor.
Middle English -yf
English -ive
English aggressive
From aggress + -ive. Compare with French agressif.

ex.en: He is so aggressive that others avoid him.
ex.ja: 彼はあまりにも性格が攻撃的で、人に避けられている。

ex.en: You have to be aggressive to be a success.
ex.ja: 出世するためには積極的な人間でなければならない。

ex.en: He assumed an aggressive attitude toward me.
ex.ja: 彼は私に攻撃的な態度をとった。

note.ja: ag（〜へ）+ gress（歩む）+ ive。〜へ攻め寄る →「攻撃的な・積極的な」。

en: Capable of being seen, or easily seen; open to view; visible to the eye; within sight or view.
Clear or manifest to the understanding; plain; evident; obvious; known; palpable; indubitable.

apparent.ety: From Middle English apparaunt, aparaunt, from Old French aparent, aparant, in turn from Latin appārēns, appārentis, present participle of appāreō.

ex.en: It was apparent that there was no way out.
ex.ja: 解決策がないのは明らかだった。

ex.en: So a new problem soon became apparent.
ex.ja: それで間もなく新たな問題が明らかになってきた。

ex.en: The company turned him down for no apparent reason.
ex.ja: その会社は確たる理由もなく、彼を不採用にしました。

note.ja: ap（〜へ）+ pare（見える）+ nt。目の前に見えている →「明らかな・見かけの」。appear（現れる）。

en: A sudden percussive noise.
A heavy strike upon an object causing such a noise.
To make sudden loud noises, often repeatedly, especially by exploding or hitting something.
To hit (something) hard, making a loud noise.
Right, directly.
Precisely, exactly, completely.
A sudden percussive sound, such as made by the firing of a gun, slamming of a door, etc.

bang.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *bangōną
Old English *bangian
Old Norse bangabor.
Middle English *bangen
English bang
From Middle English *bangen, from Old English *bangian or borrowed from Old Norse banga (“to pound, hammer”); both from Proto-Germanic *bangōną (“to beat, pound”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰen- (“to beat, hit, injure”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots bang, bung (“to strike, bang, hurl, thrash, offend”), Icelandic banga (“to pound, hammer”), Old Swedish bånga ("to hammer"; whence modern Swedish banka (“to knock, pound, bang”)), Danish banke (“to beat”), bengel (“club”), Low German

ex.en: He banged a big book on the desk.
ex.ja: 彼は大きな本をドスンと机の上に置いた。

ex.en: I got a bang out of her party.
ex.ja: 彼女のパーティーは実に楽しかった。

ex.en: Don't shut the door with a bang.
ex.ja: ドアをバタンと閉めるな。

note.ja: 擬音的な語。北欧語 banga（たたく）。「ドン」→「強打」。

en: A violent gust of wind (in windy weather) or apparent wind (around a moving vehicle).
A forcible stream of gas or liquid from an orifice, for example from a bellows, the tuyeres of a blast furnace, a person's mouth, etc.
To make an impression on, by making a loud blast or din.
To make a loud noise.
Used to show anger or disappointment: damn

blast.ety:
Inherited from Middle English blast, from Old English blǣst (“blowing, blast”), from Proto-West Germanic *blāstu, from Proto-Germanic *blēstuz (“blowing, blast”).
Cognate with West Frisian blast (“blast”), dialectal Dutch blast (“stubborn intent, drumming”), obsolete German Blast (“wind, blowing”), German blasen (“to blow”), Dutch blazen (“to blow”), Danish blæst (“wind”), French blaser (“to blunt, dull”). More at blow.

ex.en: The blast-off took place on schedule.
ex.ja: ロケットの発射は予定通り行なわれた。

ex.en: You have to blast your way out.
ex.ja: 人垣をかき分けて出なくちゃね。

ex.en: A lot of people were killed by the blast.
ex.ja: 多くの人が爆発で死んだ。

note.ja: 古英語 blǣst（突風）から。blow（吹く）と同系。「突風」→「爆発」→（口語）「とても楽しいこと」。

zh: 共產主義者 /共产主义者

en: Of, relating to, supporting, or advocating communism.
An advocate of a society based on the common ownership of property; a proponent of communism.

communist.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *mey-
Proto-Indo-European *ḱom-moy-ni-s
Proto-Italic *kommoinis
Old Latin comoinis
Latin commūnis
Old French comun
French commun
Proto-Indo-European *-id-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti
Proto-Hellenic *-íd͏̌d͏̌ō
Ancient Greek -ῐ́ζω (-ĭ́zō)
Proto-Hellenic *-tās
Ancient Greek -τής (-tḗs)
Ancient Greek -ῐστής (-ĭstḗs)bor.
Latin -istalbor.
French -iste
French communiste
English communist
From French communiste, from commun (“common, communal”) + -iste (“-ist”). By surface analysis, commune + -ist.

ex.en: I hope you'll never turn Communist.
ex.ja: 君が共産主義者にならないように希望する。

ex.en: Communists took power in China in 1949.
ex.ja: 中国では1949年に共産党が政権を取った。

ex.en: I willingly join the Chinese Communist Party.
ex.ja: 喜んで中国共産党に入ります。

note.ja: com（共に）+ mun（務め）+ ist。財産を共有する主義（communism）の人 →「共産主義者」。

en: The act of complaining.
A grievance, problem, difficulty, or concern.

complaint.ety: From Middle English compleynte, from Anglo-Norman compleint, from Old French compleindre, eventually from Latin planctus (whence plaint).

ex.en: I am sick to death of your complaints.
ex.ja: 私はあなたのぐちには死ぬほどうんざりしている。

ex.en: I'm sick of listening to your complaints.
ex.ja: 君の愚痴を聞かされるのはうんざりだ。

ex.en: I'm sick of listening to her complaints.
ex.ja: 私は彼女の不平不満を聞くのは飽き飽きした。

note.ja: complain（不平を言う）+ -t。com（強意）+ plangere（胸を打って嘆く）。「嘆き」→「苦情」。

en: The quality of being confident, not afraid or easily intimidated, but without being incautious or inconsiderate.
The ability to overcome one's fear, do or live things which one finds frightening.

courage.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *ḱerd-
Proto-Indo-European *ḱḗr ~ *ḱr̥dés
Proto-Italic *kord
Latin cor n
Latin *corem
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂tos
Proto-Italic *-ātos
Latin -ātus
Proto-Indo-European *-ikos
Proto-Italic *-ikos
Latin -icus
Latin -āticus
Latin -āticum
Vulgar Latin *corāticum
Old French coragebor.
Middle English corage
English courage
From Middle English corage, from Old French corage (French courage), from Vulgar Latin *corāticum, from Latin cor (“heart”). Distantly related to cardiac (“of the heart”)

ex.en: What you need the most now is courage.
ex.ja: 君が今一番必要なものは勇気です。

ex.en: That incident put his courage to the test.
ex.ja: その事件によって彼の勇敢さが試された。

ex.en: Your courage will come out in a crisis.
ex.ja: いざとなれば勇気が湧いてくる。

note.ja: ラテン語 cor（心）から。cour + age。心の力 →「勇気」。

en: A method, device or medication that restores good health.
An act of healing or state of being healed; restoration to health after a disease, or to soundness after injury.
To restore to health.
To bring (a disease or its bad effects) to an end.

cure.ety: From Middle English cure, borrowed from Old French cure (“care, cure, healing, cure of souls”), from Latin cura (“care, medical attendance, cure”). Displaced native Old English hǣlu, but this survived as heal.

ex.en: Cancer can be cured if discovered in time.
ex.ja: 発見が間に合えば、ガンは治療できる。

ex.en: There is no cure for the common cold.
ex.ja: ふつうのかぜに治療法はない。

ex.en: This medicine will cure you of that disease.
ex.ja: この薬を飲めばその病気は治るでしょう。

note.ja: ラテン語 cura（世話）から。世話をする →「治す・治療」。

en: In dire need (of something); having a dire need or desire.
Being filled with, or in a state of, despair; hopeless.
A person in desperate circumstances or who is at the point of desperation, such as a down-and-outer, addict, etc.

desperate.ety: From Middle English desperat(e) (“desperate”), borrowed from Latin dēspērātus, perfect passive participle of dēspērō (“to be without hope”), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix). The noun is derived from the adjective or from the Latin source through substantivization, see -ate (noun-forming suffix).

ex.en: He is in desperate search of further evidence.
ex.ja: 彼はもっと証拠がないかと、やっきになって捜している。

ex.en: He was desperate to defend his reputation.
ex.ja: 彼は名声を守ろうと必死だった。

ex.en: Tom was desperate to defend his reputation.
ex.ja: トムは自分の評判を守るのに必死だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 desperare ＝ de（離れて）+ sperare（希望する）。「希望を失った」→「絶望的な・必死の」。

en: The quality of being diverse or different; a difference or unlikeness.
A variety; diverse types or examples.

diversity.ety: From Middle English diversite, from Old French diversité, from Latin dīversitās, equivalent to diverse + -ity. Displaced native Old English mislīcnes.

ex.en: Existing legislation does not take diversity of races into account.
ex.ja: 現行の法律は人種の多様性を考慮していない。

ex.en: This forest is full of diversity.
ex.ja: この森は、多様性に富んでいます。

note.ja: di（離れて）+ vers（向ける）+ ity。別々の方向を向いていること →「多様性」。

en: The day or night before, usually used for holidays, such as Christmas Eve.
The period of time when something is just about to happen or to be introduced

eve.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der.
Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder.
Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider.
Proto-Germanic *ēbanþs
Proto-West Germanic *ābanþ
Old English ǣfen
Middle English evender.
Middle English eve
English eve
Inherited from Middle English eve, variant of even (itself from Old English ǣfen), with a pre-1200 loss of the terminal '-n'. See also the now archaic or poetic even (“evening”), from the same source.
In medieval Europe, days were considered to extend from sunset to sunset rather than midnight to midnight, so the night before a holiday was considered part of it, hence

ex.en: It is Eve that sets Adam on.
ex.ja: アダムをそそのかしたのはイブだ。

ex.en: They went to church on Christmas Eve.
ex.ja: 彼らはクリスマスイブに教会に行った。

ex.en: Are you doing anything special for New Year's Eve?
ex.ja: 大晦日には何か特別なことをするの？

note.ja: evening（夕方）の短縮。「前夜」（Christmas Eve）。

en: The academic staff at schools, colleges, universities or not-for-profit research institutes, as opposed to the students or support staff.
A division of a university.

faculty.ety: From Middle English faculte (“power, property”), from Old French faculte, from Latin facultas (“capability, ability, skill, abundance, plenty, stock, goods, property; in Medieval Latin also a body of teachers”), another form of facilitas (“easiness, facility, etc.”), from facul, another form of facilis (“easy, facile”); see facile. Doublet of facility.

ex.en: He has the faculty to learn languages easily.
ex.ja: 彼は言葉を簡単に学ぶ能力をもっている。

ex.en: He has a faculty for making other people happy.
ex.ja: 彼は他人を楽しくさせる才能を持っている。

ex.en: He has a faculty for making friends.
ex.ja: 彼は友人をつくる才能がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 facultas（できること）から。fac（する）。物事をする力 →「能力・機能」、（大学の）学部・教員。

en: Critical assessment of a process or activity or of their results.
The part of an output signal that is looped back into the input to control or modify a system.
To generate the high-frequency sound by allowing a speaker to cause vibration of the sound generator of a musical instrument connected by…
To provide informational feedback to.

feedback.ety:
Etymology tree
English feed
Proto-Indo-European *bʰeg-der.?
Proto-Germanic *baką
Proto-West Germanic *bak
Old English bæc
Middle English bak
English back
English feedback
From feed + back.

ex.en: We look forward to your feedback.
ex.ja: 僕らは君のフィードバックを楽しみしています。

ex.en: Thank you for your valuable feedback.
ex.ja: 貴重なご意見をありがとうございます。

ex.en: Please review the contents and provide any appropriate feedback.
ex.ja: 内容をご覧になり、適切なご意見をいただければ幸いです。

note.ja: feed（供給する）+ back（戻して）。出力を入力に戻すこと →「意見・反応」。

en: A person who fights; a combatant.
A warrior; a fighting soldier.

fighter.ety: From Middle English fightere, feghtere, from Old English feohtere. Equivalent to fight + -er.

ex.en: The fire fighters put out the fire.
ex.ja: 消防士は火事を消した。

ex.en: You're still a fire fighter, aren't you?
ex.ja: 今でも消防士なんでしょ？

ex.en: The fighter has taken off for a state of emergency.
ex.ja: 戦闘機は非常事態のため離陸した。

note.ja: fight（戦う）+ -er。「戦士」→「戦闘機」。

en: Especially of a liquid, to become solid due to low temperature.
To lower something's temperature to the point that it freezes or becomes hard.
A period of intensely cold weather.
A halt of a regular operation.

freeze.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *prews-der.
Proto-Germanic *-āną
Proto-Germanic *freusaną
Proto-West Germanic *freusan
Old English frēosan
Middle English fresen
English freeze
From Middle English fresen, from Old English frēosan (“to freeze”), from Proto-West Germanic *freusan, from Proto-Germanic *freusaną (“to freeze”), from Proto-Indo-European *prews- (“to freeze; frost”).
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian friis, friise, früüs (“to freeze”), Saterland Frisian fjoose, frjoze (“to freeze”), West Frisian frieze (“to freeze”), Central Franconian freese (“to freeze”), Cimbrian briizan, vrii

ex.en: How long can we keep this frozen food?
ex.ja: この冷凍食品はどのくらい保存できますか。

ex.en: What do you call it when water freezes?
ex.ja: 水が凍ったとき、それを何と呼びますか。

ex.en: She froze at the sight of the bear.
ex.ja: 彼女は熊を見かけて身がすくんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 frēosan から。frost（霜）と同じ語根。「凍る」→ 動きを「止める」。

en: Humankind; human beings as a group.
The human condition or nature.

humanity.ety: Inherited from Middle English humanyte, humanite, humanitye, from Old French humanité, from Latin hūmānitās. By surface analysis, human or humane + -ity. Partly displaced mankind, from Old English mancynn (literally “human race”).

ex.en: Nuclear weapons are a threat to all humanity.
ex.ja: 核兵器は全人類への脅威である。

ex.en: You should work in the interests of humanity.
ex.ja: 諸君は人類の利益のために働くべきだ。

ex.en: I'll do anything in the interests of humanity.
ex.ja: 人類のためになんでもするつもりだ。

note.ja: human（人間の）+ -ity。ラテン語 humanus。「人間性・人類」→ 人間を研究する「人文科学」。

en: The act of innovating; the introduction of something new, in customs, rites, etc.
A change effected by innovating; a change in customs.

innovation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French innovation, from Old French innovacion, from Late Latin innovatio, innovationem, from Latin innovo, innovatus. Morphologically innovate + -ion.

ex.en: Technological innovation brought about the rapid progress of the information industry.
ex.ja: 技術革新は情報産業に急速な進歩をもたらした。

ex.en: A company that stifles innovation can't hope to grow very much.
ex.ja: 出る杭が打たれる会社じゃ、大きな成長は望めないね。

ex.en: Open source is the engine that drives technological innovation.
ex.ja: オープンソースは技術革新をドライブするエンジンである。

note.ja: innovate（革新する）+ -ion。in + novus（新しい）。「新しくすること」。novel、renovate と同じ nov。

en: A device used to produce music.
A means or agency for achieving an aspect.
To apply measuring devices.
To devise, conceive, cook up, plan.

instrument.ety:
From Middle English instrument, from Old French instrument, from Latin īnstrūmentum (“an implement, tool”),
From īnstruō (“build, construct; arrange”) + -mentum.

ex.en: You should on no condition touch these instruments.
ex.ja: どんなことがあってもこれらの器具に触れてはならない。

ex.en: You play a musical instrument, don't you?
ex.ja: あなたは楽器を演奏しますよね。

ex.en: Do you play a musical instrument?
ex.ja: 楽器をなにか演奏しますか。

note.ja: in（中に）+ stru（積む・備える）+ ment。備えておく道具 →「器具・楽器」。

en: To spend money, time, or energy on something, especially for some benefit or purpose; used with in.
To envelop, wrap, cover.
A designated area of disturbed weather that is being monitored for potential tropical cyclone development.

invest.ety: Borrowed from Middle French investir or Medieval Latin investire, from Latin investio (“to clothe, cover”), from in- (“in, on”) + vestio (“to clothe, dress”), from vestis (“clothing”); see vest. The sense “to spend money etc.” probably via Italian investire, of the same root.

ex.en: The Prime Minister is invested with incredible powers.
ex.ja: 首相は信じられないほどの権力を与えられている。

ex.en: The government should invest more money in industry.
ex.ja: 政府は産業にもっと多くの金を投資すべきだ。

ex.en: The government should invest more money in agriculture.
ex.ja: 政府は農業にもっと投資するべきだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 investire ＝ in + vestis（衣服）。「衣服を着せる」→ 権力を着せる →（資金を）注ぎ込む →「投資する」。

en: A piece of clothing worn on the upper body outside a shirt or blouse, often waist length to thigh length.
A piece of a person's suit, beside trousers and, sometimes, waistcoat; coat (US).
To confine (someone) to a straitjacket.
To enclose or encase in a jacket or other covering.

jacket.ety: From Middle French jacquet, diminutive of Old French jaque.

ex.en: There was a black jacket on the book.
ex.ja: その本には黒いカバーがかかっていた。

ex.en: This tie and that jacket go well together.
ex.ja: このネクタイとあのジャケットはよく似合う。

ex.en: Do you have this jacket in different colors?
ex.ja: このジャケットの色違いはありますか。

note.ja: 古フランス語 jaquet（小さな上着）から。jaque（農民の上着）。

en: Making, or having the power to make, a law or laws; lawmaking.
That branch of government which is responsible for making, or having the power to make, a law or laws.

legislative.ety:
Etymology tree
English legislate
Proto-Indo-European *-wós
Proto-Indo-European *-iHwósder.
Latin -īvus
Old French -ifbor.
Middle English -yf
English -ive
English legislative
From legislate + -ive.

ex.en: Congress is the legislative branch of the government.
ex.ja: 議会は政府の立法府である。

note.ja: legislate（法を制定する）+ -ive。「立法の」。legislation と同じ。

en: Synonym of handbook.
A booklet that instructs on the usage of a particular machine or product.
Performed with the hands.
Operated by means of the hands.

manual.ety: From Middle English manuel, from Old French manuel, from Late Latin manuāle (“handbook, manual”).

ex.en: He did hard manual labor through the day.
ex.ja: 彼はその日ずっと、つらい手仕事をやった。

ex.en: Manual labor is necessary in this company.
ex.ja: この会社では肉体労働が必要です。

ex.en: We need mental skills, not manual ones.
ex.ja: 私たちに必要なのは頭の技術であって、手の技術ではない。

note.ja: man（手）+ ual。手の →「手動の・手作業の」、手元に置く本 →「説明書」。

en: To fill.
To possess or use the time or capacity of; to engage the service of.

occupy.ety: From Middle English occupien, occupyen, borrowed from Old French occuper, from Latin occupāre (“to take possession of, seize, occupy, take up, employ”), from ob (“to, on”) + capiō (“to take”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap- (“to seize, grab”). Doublet of occupate, now obsolete.

ex.en: The city was soon occupied by the soldiers.
ex.ja: その市はやがて兵隊によって占領された。

ex.en: The meeting room is occupied at the moment.
ex.ja: 会議室は現在使用中です。

ex.en: Your mind is not occupied with your own affairs.
ex.ja: 心ここにあらず、ですね。

note.ja: ラテン語 occupare ＝ ob + capere（つかむ）。「つかみ取る」→「占める・占領する」。capture と同じ cap。

en: Continuing, permanent, lasting.
Presently or currently happening; being in progress.
Something that is going on; a happening.

ongoing.ety: From on + going, related to the phrasal verb go on.

ex.en: Development is slow, but ongoing.
ex.ja: 細々とだが開発は続いている。

ex.en: The investigation is ongoing.
ex.ja: その調査は進行中です。

ex.en: The process is ongoing.
ex.ja: 現在、処理中です。

note.ja: on（続けて）+ going（進んでいる）。「進行中の」。

en: A person or organisation that operates a device, system, service, etc.
A telecommunications facilitator whose job is to connect or otherwise assist callers.

operator.ety: Borrowed from Latin operātor, from operor (“work, labour”). Equivalent to operate + -or.

ex.en: The operator put me through to New York.
ex.ja: 交換手が電話をニューヨークへつないでくれた。

ex.en: Operator, I'm trying to get through to Boston.
ex.ja: 交換台、ボストンに電話しようとしているんですが。

ex.en: This is the operator. Which extension would you like?
ex.ja: 交換手です。内線番号をどうぞ。

note.ja: operate（操作する）+ -or。ラテン語 operari（働く）、opus（仕事）。「操作者」。opera と同じ。

en: Causing pain or distress, either physical or mental.
Afflicted or suffering with pain (of a body part or, formerly, of a person).

painful.ety: From Middle English paynful, peinful, peynful, paynefull, peynefull, equivalent to pain + -ful. Compare Danish pinefuld (“painful”).

ex.en: It's painful to keep sitting for hours.
ex.ja: 何時間も座っているのは苦痛だ。

ex.en: There's nothing more painful than losing one's loved child.
ex.ja: 愛する我が子を失うことほど辛いことはない。

ex.en: That might be the most painful experience in my life.
ex.ja: 一生で一番辛い経験といえるでしょう。

note.ja: pain（痛み）+ -ful。pain はラテン語 poena（罰）。「痛い・つらい」。

en: The act of preparing or getting ready.
The state of being prepared; readiness.

preparation.ety: From Middle English preparacion, from Middle French preparacion, from Latin praeparatio, praeparationem. Morphologically prepare + -ation.

ex.en: We failed due to a lack of preparation.
ex.ja: 我々は準備不足で失敗した。

ex.en: Have you finished your preparations for the trip?
ex.ja: 旅行の準備はすべて終わりましたか。

ex.en: In preparation, clean the bath and fill it.
ex.ja: お風呂洗って、入れといてね。

note.ja: prepare（準備する）+ -ation。pre（前に）+ parare（用意する）。「準備」。repair と同じ par。

en: A hit or strike with one's fist.
Power, strength, energy.
To strike with one's fist.
To herd (cattle) as a cowboy.

punch.ety: From Middle English punchen, partially from Old French ponchonner (“to punch”), from ponchon (“pointed tool”), from Latin punctio, from punctus, perfect passive participle of pungō (“I prick”); and partially from Middle English punchen, a syncopated variant of punischen ("to punish"; see punish). Also influenced by Middle English punchon ("a punch"; see puncheon). Compare also Middle English bunchen, bonchen (“to punch, deliver a blow, pound, beat”).

ex.en: Do you want another glass of fruit punch?
ex.ja: フルーツポンチをもういっぱい欲しい？

ex.en: Oh, no! I forgot to punch in again!
ex.ja: あらいやだ。また、タイムカードを押し忘れた。

ex.en: I want to punch you in the face.
ex.ja: お前の顔を殴りたい。

note.ja: 「殴る」は古フランス語 poinçonner（穴をあける）から、ラテン語 pungere（刺す）。飲み物の「ポンチ」はヒンディー語 pāñc（5）で、5種の材料からとされ別語。

en: A colour between red and blue; violet, though often closer to magenta.
Any non-spectral colour on the line of purples on a colour chromaticity diagram or a colour wheel between violet and red.
Of a purple hue.
Not predominantly red or blue, but having a mixture of Democrat and Republican support.
To turn purple in colour.
To dye purple.

purple.ety:
From Middle English purple, purpel, from Old English purpul (“purple”, adjective), taken from Old English purpure (“purple colour”, noun), from Latin purpura (“purple dye, shellfish”), from Ancient Greek πορφύρα (porphúra, “purple-fish”), perhaps of Semitic origin. Doublet of purpura and purpure.
The sense of "imperial power" is from the wearing of the color purple by emperors and kings.

ex.en: The color is purple rather than pink.
ex.ja: その色はピンクというより紫だ。

ex.en: Red and blue paint mixed together give us purple.
ex.ja: 赤と青を混ぜると紫になる。

ex.en: If you mix blue and red, you'll get purple.
ex.ja: 青と赤を混ぜると紫になる。

note.ja: ラテン語 purpura（紫の染料を採る貝）から。古代の高価な紫の染料。

en: A permanent track consisting of fixed metal rails to drive trains or similar motorized vehicles on.
The transportation system comprising such tracks and vehicles fitted to travel on the rails, usually with several vehicles connected toge…
To transport via railroad.
To operate a railroad.

ex.en: He works on the railroad as a driver.
ex.ja: 彼は運転士として鉄道で働いている。

ex.en: The railroad workers are going on strike tomorrow.
ex.ja: 明日は鉄道がストですよ。

ex.en: There were almost no railroads out west.
ex.ja: 遠い西部にはほとんど鉄道がなかった。

note.ja: rail（線路）+ road（道）。アメリカでの「鉄道」。イギリスでは railway。

en: The act of signing up or registering for something.
That which registers or makes something official, e.g. the form or paper that registers.

ex.ja: 診察券を持って来るのを忘れてしまいました。

ex.en: Registration for the first visit is at Counter No.1.
ex.ja: 初診の受付は一番窓口です。

ex.en: YouTube registration requires a real name and an address.
ex.ja: YouTubeの登録には本名と住所が要ります。

note.ja: register（登録する）+ -ation。ラテン語 regesta（記録されたもの）、re + gerere（運ぶ）。「登録」。

zh: 浪漫的愛情 /浪漫的爱情

en: An intimate relationship between two people; a love affair.
A strong obsession or attachment for something or someone.
To woo; to court.
To write or tell romantic stories, poetry, letters, etc.

romance.ety: From Middle English romauns, roumance, borrowed from Anglo-Norman and Old French romanz, romans (the vernacular language of France, as opposed to Latin), from Medieval Latin rōmānicē, Vulgar Latin rōmānicē (“in the Roman language”, adverb), from Latin rōmānicus (“roman”, adjective) from rōmānus (“a Roman”). Doublet of Romansch.

ex.en: His romance was the talk of the town.
ex.ja: 浮き名を流したものだ。

ex.en: Can you recommend a romance novel for me?
ex.ja: おすすめの恋愛小説はありますか？

ex.en: The novelist wrote several romances.
ex.ja: その小説家は何冊かの伝奇小説を書いた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 romanz（俗語で書かれた物語）から。ラテン語ではなくローマの俗語（ロマンス語）で書かれた騎士物語 →「恋愛」。

en: To yield or give way to another.
To yield (something) to another, as when defeated.

submit.ety: From Middle English submitten, borrowed from Latin submittere, infinitive of submittō (“place under, yield”), from sub (“under, from below, up”) + mitto (“to send”). Compare upsend.

ex.en: I was forced to submit to my fate.
ex.ja: 私は運命に服従せざるを得なかった。

ex.en: He had to submit himself to their decision.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らの決定に従うほかなかった。

ex.en: Submit your term papers to Professor White.
ex.ja: 期末レポートをホワイト教授に提出せよ。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ mit（送る）。下に差し出す →「提出する・服従する」。

en: An adequate quantity of; enough.
A quantity (of something) that is as large as is needed.
Of a type or kind that suffices, that satisfies requirements or needs.
Possessing adequate talents or accomplishments; of competent power or ability; qualified; fit.

sufficient.ety: From Old French sufisanz, soficient, from Latin sufficiēns, present participle of sufficiō.

ex.en: It's not particularly wonderful, but it is sufficient.
ex.ja: 取り立ててすばらしいわけではないが満足できる。

ex.en: These are not sufficient reasons for breaking the promise.
ex.ja: これらは約束を破ったことの十分な理由にならない。

ex.en: A word to the wise is sufficient.
ex.ja: 賢者はひと言にして足る。

note.ja: suf（下から）+ fic（作る）+ ient。下から作り上げて満たす →「十分な」。

en: To halt something temporarily.
To hold in an undetermined or undecided state.

suspend.ety: From Old French sospendre, from Latin suspendere.

ex.en: Suspending the trial is out of the question.
ex.ja: 裁判を中断するのは不可能だ。

ex.en: The school principal suspended Tom for two days.
ex.ja: 学校長はトムを２日間の停学にした。

ex.en: The peace talks have been suspended for a while.
ex.ja: 和平会談はしばらく延期された。

note.ja: sus（下に）+ pend（吊るす）。下に吊るす →「吊るす・一時停止する・停学にする」。

en: Thin, woven, gauzelike fabric.
A fine transparent silk material, used for veils, etc.; specifically, cloth interwoven with gold or silver threads, or embossed with figu…
To form tissue of; to interweave.
To have the contents of an injection or intravenous drip leak into the tissue as a result of a ruptured or punctured vein.

tissue.ety: From Middle English tissu, from Old French tissu (“woven”), past participle of tistre (“to weave”), from Latin texō (“to weave”).

ex.en: I don't need a tissue.
ex.ja: ティッシュはいいよ。

ex.en: Does anyone have a tissue?
ex.ja: 誰かティッシュ持ってない？

ex.en: Give a tissue to Tom.
ex.ja: トムにティッシュをあげて。

note.ja: 古フランス語 tissu（織られたもの）から。ラテン語 texere（織る）。「薄い織物」→「ティッシュ」→ 生物の「組織」。text、texture と同じ。

en: Someone who or something that trails (follows behind); something that is trailing.
Part of an object which extends some distance beyond the main body of the object.
To load on a trailer or to transport by trailer.

trailer.ety: From trail + -er. The film sense derives from the fact that previews were formerly shown after the main feature, rather than before as is usual today, that is trailing after the main feature.

ex.en: He attached the trailer to his car.
ex.ja: 彼は自動車にトレーラーをつないだ。

ex.en: The trailer goes with the car.
ex.ja: トレーラーがその車についている。

note.ja: trail（引きずる）+ -er。「後ろに引かれるもの」→「トレーラー」→ 映画の後に流した「予告編」。

en: Below the ground; below the surface of the Earth.
Hidden, furtive, secretive.
Below the ground.
Secretly.
The regions beneath the surface of the earth, both natural (eg. caves) and man-made (eg. mines).
Synonym of subway: a railway that is under the ground.
To route electricity distribution cables underground.

ex.en: In the underground, to double-cross any member means sure death.
ex.ja: 地下組織では、仲間を裏切ることは、間違いない死を意味する。

note.ja: under（下に）+ ground（地面）。「地下の」→「秘密の」。

en: Against; in opposition to.
Compared with, as opposed to.
To face in competition
To fight

versus.ety: From Middle English versus, borrowed from Latin versus (“facing”), past participle of vertere (“to turn, change, overthrow, destroy”).

ex.en: Tonight's game is Japan versus Brazil.
ex.ja: 今夜の試合は日本対ブラジルだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 versus（〜に向かって）から。vers（向ける）。向かい合って →「〜対〜」。

en: In effect or essence, rather than in fact or reality; also, imitated, simulated.
For practical purposes, though not technically; almost complete, very near.
Preceded by the: that which is imitated or simulated rather than existing in fact or reality; (countable) an instance of this.
That which is simulated in a computer and/or online; virtual reality; (countable) an instance of this; specifically (gambling), a compute…

en: An injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear, to a (usually external) part of the body.
An injury to a person by which the skin is divided or its continuity broken.
To hurt or injure (someone) by cutting, piercing, or tearing the skin.
To hurt (a person's feelings).

wound.ety:
Noun from Middle English wund, from Old English wund, from Proto-West Germanic *wundu, from Proto-Germanic *wundō (“wound”), from Proto-Indo-European *wen- (“to strive, toil, win”).

ex.en: Stop the flow of blood from the wound.
ex.ja: 傷から流れる血を止めなさい。

ex.en: Many men were badly wounded in the battle.
ex.ja: 多くの兵士が戦いでひどいケガを負った。

ex.en: The wounded soldiers were left in the field.
ex.ja: 負傷兵達は戦場に取り残された。

note.ja: 古英語 wund から。「傷」。wind（巻く）の過去形 wound は別語で発音も違う。

en: Denotes a mingling or intermixing with distinct or separable objects. See usage note at amidst.

amongst.ety: From amongs + -t (excrescent), from among + -s (genitive). By surface analysis, among + -st (excrescent). Root among from Old English ongemang, from on (“in”) + gemang (“assemblage, mingling”).

ex.en: I don't like families that quarrel amongst themselves.
ex.ja: お互いに言い争いをする家族は嫌いです。

ex.en: Angels watch from above as men fight amongst themselves.
ex.ja: 人間同士が戦うところを天使が空から眺めている。

ex.en: Find life amongst death.
ex.ja: 死中に活を求める。

note.ja: among の古い形に -st がついた語。主にイギリスで使う。

en: An act of announcing, or giving notice.
That which conveys what is announced.

announcement.ety: From Middle French annoncement. By surface analysis, announce + -ment.

ex.en: We should have paid attention to the announcement.
ex.ja: 私達はその発表に注意を払うべきだった。

ex.en: The prime minister will make an announcement tomorrow.
ex.ja: 首相は明日声明を出すことになっている。

ex.en: The announcement was a surprise and very exciting.
ex.ja: 発表会はサプライズで沸き立った。

note.ja: announce（発表する）+ -ment。ad + nuntiare（知らせる）。「発表」。pronounce と同じ。

To plan; to prepare in advance.

ex.ja: 生け花を習いたいんです。

en: A military establishment for the storing, development, manufacturing, testing, or repairing of arms, ammunition, and other war materiel; …
A stock of weapons, especially all the weapons that a nation possesses.

arsenal.ety: From Italian arsenale, from Arabic دَار الصِّنَاعَة (dār aṣ-ṣināʕa, “manufacturing shop”), from دَار (dār) + صِنَاعَة (ṣināʕa).

ex.en: The army surrendered its arsenal to the enemy.
ex.ja: 軍は敵に弾薬庫を引き渡した。

note.ja: アラビア語 dār aṣ-ṣināʿa（工作所）からイタリア語を経た語。「造兵廠・兵器庫」→「（手段の）蓄え」。

en: To pull toward without touching.
To draw by moral, emotional or sexual influence; to engage or fix, as the mind, attention, etc.; to invite or allure.

attract.ety: From Latin attractus, past participle of attrahere (“to draw to, attract”), from ad (“to”) + trahere (“to draw”).

ex.en: The magic of his words attracted the audience.
ex.ja: 彼のことばの魔力が聴衆を魅了した。

ex.en: They attract customers by offering high-quality goods.
ex.ja: 彼らは高品質の商品を提供する事によって顧客を引き付けている。

ex.en: Her clothes attracted much attention at the party.
ex.ja: 彼女の服はパーティーでおおいに注意をひいた。

note.ja: at（〜へ）+ tract（引く）。〜へ引きつける →「引きつける・魅了する」。

Relating to anatomy; anatomic, anatomical.

ex.ja: メアリーはトムの実の母です。

To hold something by clamping one's teeth.
The act of biting.
The wound left behind after having been bitten.

ex.ja: 自分の犬に噛まれたことってある？

A damaged area of a surface where a small piece has been broken off.
To chop or cut into small pieces.
To break small pieces from.

ex.ja: ピアノの月謝ちょうだい。

en: Commendation; favourable representation in words.
Worship, glorification, adoration.
To give praise to; to commend, glorify, or worship.

praise.ety: From Middle English praise, preyse, from the verb (see below). Doublet of prize. Displaced native Middle English lof from Old English lof (“praise”) and Middle English loenge, loange from Old French löenge, löange (“praise”).

ex.en: All parents like to have their children praised.
ex.ja: すべての親は自分の子供がほめられるのを好む。

ex.en: We cannot praise him highly enough for this.
ex.ja: この事で彼をいくらほめてもまだ足りない。

ex.en: The boss praised you for your good work.
ex.ja: 社長があなたのことをよく働くといって誉めていました。

note.ja: 古フランス語 preisier（値をつける）から。ラテン語 pretium（値段）。「価値を認める」→「ほめる」。price、precious と同じ。

en: The act of presenting, or something presented.
The outward appearance or representation of a person or thing to the human mind.

presentation.ety: From Old French presentation (French présentation), from Latin praesentātiōnem, accusative singular of praesentātiō (“representation, exhibition”). Morphologically present + -ation.

ex.en: It was a successful presentation of a play.
ex.ja: 成功を収めた劇の上映。

ex.en: I made them look good at the big presentation.
ex.ja: 注目を集めた発表会で彼らに花を持たせた。

ex.en: I felt passion from that good presentation.
ex.ja: 熱意が感じられる良いプレゼンだった。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ sent（ある）+ ation。目の前に差し出すこと →「発表・提示・贈呈」。

en: The study of the human mind.
The study of human or animal behavior.

psychology.ety: From French psychologie, from Renaissance Latin psychologia, from Ancient Greek ψυχή (psukhḗ, “soul”) + -λογία (-logía, “study of”), equivalent to psycho- + -logy. The Latin term is believed by some to have been coined in a lost treatise by Croatian humanist Marko Marulić (1450–1524), but this is disputed by other scholars. It is first attested in the 1570s, at which time it was apparently already current, and may be a Hellenization of the established expression dē animā (“on the soul”) in titles.

ex.en: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind.
ex.ja: 心理学は心を科学研究する学問である。

ex.en: I can't understand the psychology of such a man.
ex.ja: 私にはそんな男の心理は理解できません。

ex.en: I have studied Psychology to some extent.
ex.ja: 私は、ある程度まで心理学を勉強しました。

note.ja: psych（心）+ o + log（学問）+ y。心の学問 →「心理学・心理」。

en: The act of restricting, or the state of being restricted.
A regulation or limitation that restricts.

restriction.ety:
From Middle English restriccioun, from Anglo-Norman restriction, Middle French restriction, and their source, Late Latin restrictiō, from Latin restringō.
Morphologically restrict + -ion.

ex.en: We should not put restrictions on foreign trade.
ex.ja: 外国貿易に制限を加えるべきではない。

ex.en: They decided to abolish the old restriction.
ex.ja: 彼らは古い規制を廃止することを決めた。

ex.en: Critics are coming down hard on tightened economic restrictions.
ex.ja: 評論家たちは経済規制の強化を激しく非難しています。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ strict（締める）+ ion。引き締めること →「制限」。

en: A cylindrical projectile that can be fired to a great height through combustion, (specifically) a type of firework of this form, typicall…
A blunt lance head used in jousting.
To accelerate swiftly and powerfully.
To fly vertically.

rocket.ety:
From Italian rocchetta, from Old Italian rocchetto (“rocket”, literally “a bobbin”), diminutive of rocca (“a distaff”), from Lombardic rocko (“spinning wheel”), from Proto-West Germanic *rokkō, from Proto-Germanic *rukkô (“a distaff, a staff with flax fibres tied loosely to it, used in spinning thread”). Cognate with Old High German rocco, rocko, roccho, rocho ("a distaff"; > German Rocken (“a distaff”)), Swedish rock (“a distaff”), Icelandic rokkur (“a distaff”), Middle English rocke (“a distaff”). For the meaning development, compare fuselage, ultimately from Latin fūsus (“spi

ex.ja: 月ロケットが今晩打ち上げられるだろう。

ex.en: I went to space on a rocket.
ex.ja: ロケットで宇宙に行った。

note.ja: イタリア語 rocchetta（小さな糸巻き）から。形が似ていたことから。

en: The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.
The state of being a ruin, destroyed or decayed.
To cause the fiscal ruin of; to bankrupt or drive out of business.
To destroy or render something no longer usable or operable.

ruin.ety: From Middle English ruyne, ruine, from Old French ruine, from Latin ruīna (“overthrow, ruin”), from ruō (“to fall down, tumble, sink in ruin, rush”).

ex.en: He ruined his health by working too much.
ex.ja: 仕事のしすぎで彼は体を壊した。

ex.en: He ruined his body by drinking too much.
ex.ja: 彼は酒を飲みすぎて体をだめにした。

ex.en: He ruined his health by working too hard.
ex.ja: 彼は働きすぎて体を壊した。

note.ja: ラテン語 ruina（崩れ落ちること）から。ruere（崩れる）。「破滅」→「廃墟」。

A drudge; one who labors or is obliged (e.g. by prior contract) to labor like a slave with limited rights, e.g. an indentured servant.
To work as a slaver, to enslave people.
To work hard.

en: The condition of being stable or in equilibrium, and thus resistant to change.
The tendency to recover from perturbations.

stability.ety: From Middle English stabletee, stabilite, from Old French stabilité, from Latin root of stabilitas (“firmness, steadfastness”), from stabilis (“steadfast, firm”). Displaced native Old English staþolfæstnes.

ex.en: I want stability in my life.
ex.ja: 生活を安定させたい。

ex.en: Lying related to sexual psychology development, mental stability and knowledge.
ex.ja: 嘘は知能、性心理の発達や精神の安定に関係している。

note.ja: stable（安定した）+ -ity。ラテン語 stare（立つ）。「安定」。stand、status と同じ sta。

en: Firm in standing or position; not tottering or shaking; fixed; firm.
Constant in feeling, purpose, or pursuit; not fickle, changeable, or wavering; not easily moved or persuaded to alter a purpose; resolute.
To stabilize; to prevent from shaking.
To become stable.
Aspect marker indicating consistency or intensity.
A rest or support, as for the hand, a tool, or a piece of work.
A regular boyfriend or girlfriend; somebody to go steady with.

steady.ety:
From Middle English stedy, studi, stidiȝ, perhaps continuing Old English stæþþiġ, ġestæþþiġ (“steadfast, stable, firm, staid”), equivalent to stead + -y; or calquing Middle Low German or Middle Dutch stēdig. Cognate with Saterland Frisian stoadig (“steady”), West Frisian stadich (“slow”), Danish stedig, stadig, steeg, Swedish stadig, Icelandic stöðugur, German stätig, stetig.
Compare also Old English ġestedegian (“to bring to a standstill”) and Dutch steeds (“more and more”).
Adjective sense 8 is a semantic loan from Singapore Hokkien 在 (chāi, “confident, skilled”, literally “steady”).

ex.en: He maintained a steady speed on the highway.
ex.ja: 彼は高速道路で一定のスピードを維持した。

ex.en: I thought you were going steady with Tom.
ex.ja: トムと付き合っているんだと思ってた。

ex.en: You've got to get a steady job.
ex.ja: まともな仕事につかなければいけませんよ。

note.ja: stead（場所）+ -y。「その場所にしっかりある」→「安定した・着実な」。instead と同じ stead。

A thing considered the embodiment or cardinal exemplar of a concept, theme, or other thing.
To symbolize.

en: A building in an airport where passengers transfer from ground transportation to the facilities that allow them to board airplanes.
A harbour facility where ferries embark and disembark passengers and load and unload vehicles.
Fatal; resulting in death.
Appearing at the end; top or apex of a physical object.
To store bulk liquids (such as oil or chemicals) in storage tanks prior to further distribution.

ex.ja: 私は始発駅で電車に乗る。

en: A room, enclosed area or single-purpose building containing a fixture or fixtures used for urination and defecation; a bathroom or water …
A small secondary lavatory having a fixture used for urination and defecation and sink but no bathtub or shower.
To use (urinate or defecate in) a toilet.
To assist another (a child, etc.) in using a toilet.

toilet.ety: From Middle French toilette, diminutive of toile (“cloth”), from their use to protect clothing while shaving or arranging hair. From its use as a private room, toilet came to refer euphemistically to lavatories and then to its fixtures, beginning in the United States in the late 19th century.

ex.en: Is there a public toilet in this building?
ex.ja: この建物には公衆トイレがありますか。

ex.en: I run to the toilet every thirty minutes.
ex.ja: ３０分おきにトイレに行きます。

ex.en: Let's wash our hands when leaving the toilet!
ex.ja: トイレから出たら手を洗いましょう！

note.ja: フランス語 toilette（小さな布）から。身支度の台にかけた布 →「身支度」→「化粧室」→「トイレ」。

en: A formal binding agreement concluded by subjects of international law, namely, states and international organizations; a convention, a pact.
To get into (a specific situation) through a treaty.
To enter into a treaty.

ex.ja: これが平和条約の草案だ。

ex.en: In 1978 a peace treaty was concluded between Japan and China.
ex.ja: １９７８年に日本と中国との間に平和条約が結ばれた。

note.ja: ラテン語 tractare（扱う）から。取り扱いについての取り決め →「条約」。

Of three times the quantity; treble.
Three times or thrice the number, amount, size, etc.
A drink with three portions of alcohol.
To multiply by three.
To get a three-base hit.

ex.ja: トムは三塁打を打った。

note.ja: ラテン語 triplus（3倍の）から。tri（3）+ -plus（〜倍）。double、quadruple と同じ作り。

en: Not likely; improbable; not to be reasonably expected.
Not holding out a prospect of success; likely to fail; unpromising.
In an improbable manner.
Something or somebody considered unlikely.

unlikely.ety: From Middle English unlykely, unlikly, unlykly, unlicli. By surface analysis, un- + likely.

ex.ja: 植物が痛みを感じるなんてあり得ないと思う。

ex.en: This story sounds very unlikely to me.
ex.ja: この話はどうも私にはありそうもないように聞こえる。

ex.en: That story of his sounds very unlikely.
ex.ja: 彼のあの話はまゆつばものだ。

A list of matters to be taken up (as at a meeting).
To add (an item) to an official schedule.

ex.ja: では次の議題に移りましょう。

en: Any flying mammal of the order Chiroptera, usually small and nocturnal, insectivorous or frugivorous.
To hit with a bat or (figuratively) as if with a bat.
To take a turn at hitting a ball with a bat in sports like cricket, baseball and softball, as opposed to fielding.

bat.ety: Variant of Middle English bakke, of North Germanic origin (akin to Danish aftenbakke and Swedish nattbacka, both now dialectal). Swedish also has nattblacka, and Icelandic has leðurblaka, in which the second element is a derivative of blaka (“to flap”), but it is unclear whether this word is also the source of bakke, backa, etc.

ex.ja: 少年はバットを小脇に抱えている。

To play music on (a stringed) instrument using a bow.

en: Any system by which time is divided into days, weeks, months, and years.
A means to determine the date consisting of a document containing dates and other temporal information.
To set a date for a proceeding in court, usually done by a judge at a calendar call.
To enter or write in a calendar; to register.

ex.ja: カレンダーの日付は１９６４年９月２３日でした。

ex.en: I hang the calendar on the wall.
ex.ja: 私は壁にカレンダーを掛ける。

ex.en: "Is today Wednesday?" "Look at the calendar."
ex.ja: 「今日って、水曜だっけ？」「カレンダー見なよ」

en: A piece or point of land, extending beyond the adjacent coast into a sea or lake; a promontory; a headland.
To incite or attract (a bull) to charge a certain direction, by waving a cape.
To head or point; to keep a course.

cape.ety:
From Middle English cape, gappe, cap, from Old French cap (“cape, headland”), from Latin caput (“head”). Compare Old Norse kobbi (“islet, small cape”).

ex.ja: そこでは岬が海に突き出している。

ex.en: The ship sailed around the cape.
ex.ja: その船は岬を回った。

ex.ja: トラは猫より大きくて強い。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 tigris から。イランの言葉に由来するとされる。チグリス川（矢のように速い川）と同じ語とされる。

en: Something to play with, especially as intended for use by a child.
A thing of little importance or value; a trifle.
To play (with) in an idle or desultory way.
To ponder or consider.
Impractical or unsuitable for real-world use, due to being unrealistically small or simple.

toy.ety:
Inherited from Middle English toye (“amorous play, piece of fun or entertainment”), probably from Middle Dutch toy, tuyg (“tools, apparatus, utensil, ornament”) as in Dutch speel-tuig (“plaything, toy”), from Old Dutch *tiug, from Proto-West Germanic *tiugī̆, *teug, from Proto-Germanic *teugą (“stuff, matter, device, gear, lever”, literally “that which is drawn or pulled”), from Proto-Germanic *teuhaną (“to lead, bring, pull”), from Proto-Indo-European *dewk- (“to pull, lead”).
Cognate with Dutch tuig (“thing”), German Zeug (“stuff”), Danish tøj (“stuff”), Icelandic tygi, Norwegian tøy (“equip

ex.en: Such toys have a bad influence on children.
ex.ja: このようなおもちゃは子どもに悪い影響がある。

ex.en: The toy department is on the fifth floor.
ex.ja: おもちゃ売り場は５階です。

ex.en: No, not how many toys, how many keys?
ex.ja: いいえ、おもちゃがいくつあるかじゃなくて、鍵がいくつあるかなのよ。

note.ja: 中英語 toye（遊び・戯れ）から。語源ははっきりしない。

en: A person who is actively engaged in battle, conflict or warfare; a soldier or combatant.
A person who is aggressively, courageously, or energetically involved in an activity, such as athletics.

warrior.ety: From Middle English werreour, from Anglo-Norman werreur, Old French guerroiier (“fighter, combattant”), from Medieval Latin werra, from Frankish *werʀu (“confusion; quarrel”), from Proto-Indo-European *wers- (“to mix up, confuse, beat, thresh”). Displaced earlier Old English cempa and many others.

ex.en: Summer grasses, all that remain of warriors' dreams.
ex.ja: 夏草や兵どもが夢の跡。

ex.en: The chief massed his warriors to attack the fort.
ex.ja: 酋長はとりでを攻撃するために戦士を集結させた。

ex.en: Easy living corrupted the warrior spirit.
ex.ja: 安逸の生活が軍人精神をだめにした。

note.ja: 古フランス語 werreieor（戦う人）から。werre（戦争）。war と同じ語。

en: An element of personal character that enables one to distinguish the wise from the unwise.
A piece of wise advice.

wisdom.ety: From Middle English wisdom, from Old English wīsdōm (“wisdom”), from Proto-West Germanic *wīsadōm, from Proto-Germanic *wīsadōmaz (“wisdom”), corresponding to wise + -dom. Cognate with Scots wisdom, wysdom (“wisdom”), West Frisian wiisdom (“wisdom”), Dutch wijsdom (“wisdom”), German Weistum (“legal sentence”), Danish/Norwegian/Swedish visdom (“wisdom”), Icelandic vísdómur (“wisdom”).

ex.en: He had enough wisdom to refuse the offer.
ex.ja: 彼にはその申し出を断るだけの分別があった。

ex.en: She had enough wisdom to refuse the offer.
ex.ja: 彼女には申し出を断るだけの分別があった。

ex.en: She had the wisdom to follow the custom.
ex.ja: 彼女は賢明にもそこの、風習に従った。

note.ja: wise（賢い）+ -dom。「知恵」。

en: A person, animal, plant, or other thing which is from outside the family, group, organization, or territory under consideration.
A citizen or national of another sovereign state.
Not belonging to the same country, land, or government, or to the citizens or subjects thereof; foreign.
Very unfamiliar, strange, or removed.
To estrange; to alienate.
To transfer the ownership of something.

alien.ety: From Middle English alien, a borrowing from Old French alien, aliene, from Latin aliēnus (“belonging to someone else”, later “exotic, foreign”), from Latin alius (“other”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos. Related to English else.

ex.en: It had an effect alien from the one intended.
ex.ja: 意図していたものとかけ離れた結果となった。

ex.en: Those ideas are alien to our way of thinking.
ex.ja: そのような考えは我々の考えとは相容れない。

ex.en: Your methods are totally alien to mine.
ex.ja: あのやり方は私のやり方とは性質が全く違っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 alienus（他人の）から。ali（他の）+ en。よその →「外国の・異質な・宇宙人」。

en: Lacking dexterity in the use of the hands or of tools.
Not easily managed; embarrassing.
Someone or something that is awkward.

awkward.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *-o
Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó
Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ-

From awk (“odd, clumsy”) + -ward. Compare Middle English aukeward (“in the wrong direction”).

ex.en: There was an awkward silence when he appeared.
ex.ja: 彼が現れると気まずい沈黙が広がった。

ex.en: I feel awkward in his presence.
ex.ja: あの人は煙たい。

ex.en: His words created an awkward situation.
ex.ja: 彼の言葉が困った事態を引き起こした。

note.ja: 北欧語 afugr（逆向きの）+ -ward（方向）。「逆向きの」→「ぎこちない・気まずい」。

en: Any four-footed land mammal.
All non-human animals seen as a group.
To impose arduous exercise upon, either as training or as punishment.

beast.ety: From Middle English beeste, beste, from Old French beste (French bête), from Latin bēstia (“animal, beast”); many cognates – see bēstia.

ex.en: Then the wild beasts start wanting to go crazy.
ex.ja: それから野獣がクレイジーになりたがり始める。

ex.en: The food was not fit for man or beast.
ex.ja: その食事は人間や動物に適さないものだった。

ex.en: For man, there is no beast more scary than man.
ex.ja: 人にとって人以上に恐怖となる獣は世界に存在しない。

note.ja: ラテン語 bestia（獣）から古フランス語を経た語。beastly、bestial と同じ。

en: The meat from cattle or other bovines; especially, that from adults.
The edible portions of a cow (including those which are not meat).
To cry.
Being a bovine animal that is being raised for its meat.
Producing or known for raising lots of beef.

beef.ety:
From Middle English beef, bef, beof, borrowed from Anglo-Norman beof, Old French buef, boef (“ox”) (modern French bœuf); from Latin bovem (“ox”), from Proto-Italic *gʷōs, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷṓws. Doublet of cow.
Beef in the sense of “a grudge, argument” was originally an American slang expression:
* attested as a verb “to complain” in 1888: “He'll beef an' kick like a steer an' let on he won't never wear 'em.”— New York World, 13 May;
* attested as a noun “complaint, protest, grievance, sim.” in 1899: “He made a Horrible Beef because he couldn't get Loaf Sugar for his Coffee

ex.en: The Japanese eat more beef than the British do.
ex.ja: 日本人はイギリス人より牛肉を食べる。

ex.en: He doesn't like beef. Neither do I.
ex.ja: 彼は牛肉が好きではありません。私もです。

ex.en: The ground beef was found to contain horse meat.
ex.ja: 牛ミンチに馬肉が混入しているのが見つかりました。

note.ja: ラテン語 bos（牛）から古フランス語 boef を経た語。生きた cow はゲルマン語、食卓の beef はフランス語由来（pig と pork も同じ関係）。

en: Crystallized sugar formed by boiling down sugar syrup.
Edible, sweet-tasting confectionery containing sugar, or sometimes artificial sweeteners, and often flavored with fruit, chocolate, nuts,…
To cook in or coat with sugar syrup.
To form into congelations or crystals, especially of sugar or syrup.

candy.ety: From Middle English sugre candy, from Old French sucre candi (literally “candied sugar”), from Arabic سُكَّر قَنْدِي (sukkar qandī), from Arabic قَنْد (qand, “rock candy”), from Persian کند (kand) from Sanskrit खण्ड (khaṇḍa, “piece, fragment, candied sugar, dried molasses”), root खण्ड् (khaṇḍ, “to divide, break into pieces”), or from Proto-Dravidian *kaṇṭu; compare Tamil கண்டு (kaṇṭu, “hard candy”).

ex.en: My son took a candy from the box.
ex.ja: 息子は箱から飴を一つ取った。

ex.en: This shop has more candy than that shop.
ex.ja: この店にはあの店よりたくさんのお菓子があります。

ex.en: Take care not to eat too much candy.
ex.ja: 飴を食べ過ぎないように。

note.ja: sugar candy の短縮。アラビア語 qandī（砂糖の）、サンスクリット語 khaṇḍa（砂糖の塊）。

en: A person or object that carries someone or something else.
A starship designed to carry starfighters

carrier.ety: From Middle English cariere, partly from carien + -ere, after Anglo-Norman carier, cariour, and partly directly from Anglo-Norman. By surface analysis, carry + -er.

ex.en: The mail carrier is bound to come soon.
ex.ja: もうじき郵便屋さんが来るはずです。

ex.en: The letter carrier is bound to come soon.
ex.ja: もうじき郵便屋さんが来るはずです。

ex.en: The letter carrier comes every three days.
ex.ja: 郵便配達は２日おきにやって来ます。

note.ja: carry（運ぶ）+ -er。「運ぶもの」→「運送会社・航空会社・保菌者・空母」。

en: The formal performance of a solemn rite, such as Christian sacrament.
The observance of a holiday or feast day, as by solemnities.

celebration.ety: From Old French celebration, from Latin celebratio. Equivalent to celebrate + -ion.

ex.en: Please accept this gift for the celebration on your wedding.
ex.ja: 結婚のお祝いに、これをお贈りします。

ex.en: We gave a party in celebration of his 70th birthday.
ex.ja: 彼の７０歳の誕生日を祝ってパーティーを開いた。

ex.en: As a celebration, I wonder if I should cook red rice or something?
ex.ja: お祝いに赤飯でも炊こうかしら。

note.ja: celebrate（祝う）+ -ion。「祝賀」。

en: Fame, renown; the state of being famous or talked-about.
A person who has a high degree of recognition by the general population for his or her success or accomplishments; a famous person.

celebrity.ety: From Middle English celebritē, from Old French celebrite (compare French célébrité), from Latin celēbritās.

ex.en: He is something of a celebrity.
ex.ja: 彼はちょっとした有名人です。

ex.en: On encountering the celebrity, they asked for his autograph.
ex.ja: 彼らは有名人と出くわすなり、サインをもとめた。

ex.en: On encountering the celebrity, the fans asked for his autograph.
ex.ja: ファン達は有名人と出くわすなり、彼にサインを求めた。

note.ja: ラテン語 celebritas（大勢の集まり・名声）から。celeber（人の多い）。「名声」→「有名人」。celebrate と同じ。

en: A document containing a certified statement.
A document evidencing ownership or debt.
To supply with a certificate, especially following certification.
Certified, assured.

certificate.ety: The noun is from Middle English certificat, certificate, sertyfycat, from Middle French certificat or its etymon Medieval Latin certificātum. The verb is from the noun. The adjective is a learned borrowing from Latin certificātus.

ex.en: If you have a medical certificate, bring it.
ex.ja: もし診断書があったらお待ちください。

ex.en: This certificate is valid until the end of 2023.
ex.ja: この証明書は令和5年末まで有効です。

ex.en: You shall receive two certificates of achievement.
ex.ja: 二つの修得証書を与えよう。

note.ja: ラテン語 certificare ＝ certus（確かな）+ facere（する）。「確かにする書類」→「証明書」。certain、certify と同じ。

en: To quote; to repeat, as a passage from a book, or the words of another.
To mention; to make mention of.
A citation.

cite.ety: From Old French citer, from Latin citare (“to cause to move, excite, summon”), frequentative of ciēre (“to rouse, excite, call”). Sense 4 is the original one.

ex.en: She would cite from the Bible.
ex.ja: 彼女はよく聖書から引用したものだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 citare（呼び出す・動かす）から。「（証人を）呼び出す」→「引用する・挙げる」。excite、recite と同じ cit。

en: A mineral substance made up of small crystals of silica and alumina, that is ductile when moist; the material of pre-fired ceramics.
An earth material with ductile qualities.
To add clay to, to spread clay onto.
To purify using clay.

clay.ety:

English clay
From Middle English cley, clay, from Old English clǣġ (“clay”), from Proto-West Germanic *klaij, from Proto-Germanic *klajjaz (“clay”), derived from Proto-Indo-European *gleyH- (“to glue, paste, stick together”). Cognate with Dutch klei (“clay”), Low German Klei (“clay”), German Klei, Danish klæg (“clay”); compare Ancient Greek γλία (glía), Latin glūten (“glue”) (whence ultimately English glue), Rus

ex.en: He formed the clay into a bowl.
ex.ja: 彼は粘土で鉢をつくった。

ex.en: They lived in a little clay house.
ex.ja: 彼らはこぢんまりとした土壁の家で暮らしていました。

ex.en: Tom worked the clay into a vase.
ex.ja: トムは粘土で花瓶を作った。

note.ja: 古英語 clǣg から。glue（のり）と同系で「くっつくもの」。

en: A fellow member of a profession, staff, academic faculty or other organization; an associate, a workmate.
To unite or associate with another or with others.

colleague.ety: From Middle French collegue, from Latin collēga (“a partner in office”), from com- (“with”) + lēgō (“to send on an embassy”), from lēx (“law”).

ex.en: He made the plan along with his colleagues.
ex.ja: 彼は同僚と一緒にその計画を作った。

ex.en: He planned the project along with his colleagues.
ex.ja: 彼は同僚と協力してその計画を立てた。

ex.en: One of my colleagues gave me a gift.
ex.ja: 同僚からお土産をもらいました。

note.ja: ラテン語 collega ＝ com（共に）+ legare（任命する）。「共に任命された人」→「同僚」。college と同じ。

en: Something constructed from parts.
A concept or model.
To build or form (something) by assembling parts.
To build (a sentence, an argument, etc.) by arranging words or ideas.

construct.ety: Borrowed from Latin cōnstrūctus, from cōnstruō (“to heap together”), from com- (“together”) + struō (“to heap up, pile”). Doublet of construe.

ex.en: The factory was constructed out of concrete.
ex.ja: その工場はコンクリートで建造された。

ex.en: I wonder when this building was constructed.
ex.ja: いったいこの建物はいつ建設されたのだろう。

ex.en: It is said that a new restaurant was constructed.
ex.ja: 新しいレストランが出来たそうだ。

note.ja: con（共に）+ struct（積む）。積み重ねて組み立てる →「建設する・組み立てる・構成概念」。

en: The condition of failing to meet an obligation.
The condition of being an obligation that has not been met.
To fail to appear and answer a summons and complaint.
To fail to fulfill a financial obligation.

default.ety: From Middle English defaut, defaute, from Old French defaute (“fault, defect, failure, culpability, lack”), ultimately from Latin de- (“away”) + fallo (“deceive, cheat, escape notice of”).

ex.en: Are you using the default settings?
ex.ja: 初期設定のまま使ってるの？

note.ja: 古フランス語 defaute（欠けていること）から。de + fallere（欠ける）。「義務を欠くこと」→「債務不履行」→ 指定がないときの「初期設定」。fault と同じ。

en: To obtain or receive (something) from something else.
To deduce (a conclusion) by reasoning.

derive.ety: From Middle English deriven, from Old French deriver, from Latin dērīvō (“to lead, turn, or draw off (a liquid), draw off, derive”), from dē (“away”) + rīvus (“a stream”); see rival. Unrelated to arrive.

ex.en: You will derive great benefits from learning English.
ex.ja: 英語の学習から大いに利益を得るだろう。

ex.en: Some people derive pleasure from watching horror movies.
ex.ja: ホラー映画を見ることに楽しみを見いだす人もいる。

ex.en: These words are derived from the same root.
ex.ja: これらの語は同じ語源から出ている。

note.ja: ラテン語 derivare ＝ de（〜から）+ rivus（小川）。「川から水を引く」→「引き出す・由来する」。river、rival と同系。

dialog.ety: Variant of dialogue. Equivalent to dia- + -log or di- + -alog.

ex.en: The writer is very good at a dialog.
ex.ja: その作家は会話を書くのがうまい。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 dialogos（対話）＝ dia（通して）+ logos（言葉）。「言葉を交わすこと」。

en: Made incapable of use or action.
Having a disability.

ex.en: I really enjoy helping disabled people.
ex.ja: 身体障害者を助けるのが本当に楽しいのです。

ex.en: That poor lady is disabled.
ex.ja: あの女性は気の毒にからだが不自由だ。

ex.en: My account is still disabled.
ex.ja: 私のアカウントはまだ使えない。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ abled（できる）。「障がいのある」→ 機能が「無効にされた」。

en: Capable of being perceived very clearly.
Different from one another (with the preferable adposition being "from").

distinct.ety: From Middle English distincte, past participle of distincten (“to distinguish, discern”), from Old French destincter, from Latin distinctus, past participle of distinguere (“to distinguish”); see distinguish.

ex.en: It's quite distinct from the smell of burning.
ex.ja: それは焦げている臭いとは全然違う。

ex.en: We are distinct from each other in taste.
ex.ja: 私達は趣味がまったく違うのだ。

ex.en: Your way of thinking is quite distinct from mine.
ex.ja: 君の考えは僕の考えとまるで違う。

note.ja: ラテン語 distinctus（区別された）から。distinguere（刺して印をつける・区別する）。「はっきり区別された」。distinguish と同じ。

en: Resistance of a fluid to something moving through it.
Any force acting in opposition to the motion of an object.
To pull along a surface or through a medium, sometimes with difficulty.
To proceed heavily, laboriously, or slowly; to advance with weary effort; to go on lingeringly.

From Middle English draggen (“to drag”), early Middle English dragen (“to draw, carry”), confluence of Old English dragan (“to drag, draw, draw oneself, go, protract”) and Old Norse draga (“to draw, attract”); both from Proto-Germanic *draganą (“to draw, drag”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰregʰ- (“to draw, drag”).
Verb sense influenced due to association with the noun

ex.en: The meeting on sales promotion is dragging on.
ex.ja: 販売促進に関する会議が延々と続いている。

ex.en: Today I dragged my mother out for shopping.
ex.ja: 今日母を買い物に引っ張って行きました。

ex.en: She half dragged, half carried the log.
ex.ja: 彼女はその丸太を半ば引きずるように、半ば抱えるようにして運んだ。

note.ja: 古北欧語 draga（引く）から。draw と同系。「引きずる」→ 引きずるように「長引く」。

en: To instruct or train.

educate.ety: From Middle English educaten, from educat(e) (“educated”, also used as the past participle of educaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), from Latin ēducātus, the perfect passive participle of ēducō (“(of a child, physically or mentally) to bring up, train, nourish; (of a person in learning or art) to rear, educate, train; (plants or animals) to nourish, support, or produce”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), further from an intensive/frequentative formed on ēducō (“lead out, draw out; to raise up, erect”) + -ō.

ex.en: All educated Americans, first or last, go to Europe.
ex.ja: 全ての教養あるアメリカ人は最初かまたは最後にヨーロッパに行く。

ex.en: He was educated at a public school.
ex.ja: 彼は公立学校で教育を受けた。

ex.en: He is proud of having been educated in Paris.
ex.ja: 彼はパリで教育を受けたことを自慢している。

note.ja: ラテン語 educare（育てる）から。e（外へ）+ ducere（導く）。「能力を引き出す」→「教育する」。

en: Allowed to and meeting the necessary conditions required to participate in or be chosen for something.
Worthy of being chosen (for marriage).
One who is eligible.

eligible.ety: From Middle French eligible, from Latin eligibilis, from ēligō (“to select, to choose”).

ex.en: Tom says that he isn't eligible to vote.
ex.ja: トムは彼には投票権がないと言う。

ex.en: She is not eligible for marriage.
ex.ja: 彼女は、結婚の資格はない。

ex.en: Mr Frost is eligible for the post.
ex.ja: フロスト氏はその地位につく資格がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 eligere（選び出す）から。e + legere（選ぶ）。「選ばれる資格のある」。elect、elite と同じ。

en: The act, manner or style of executing (actions, maneuvers, performances).
The state of being accomplished.

execution.ety: From Old French execution (c.1360), from Latin exsecutiō, an agent noun from exsequor (“to follow out”), from ex (“out”) + sequor (“follow”). Equivalent to execute + -ion.

ex.en: The plan was good, but its execution was poor.
ex.ja: 計画はよかったが、その実行がまずかった。

note.ja: execute（実行する）+ -ion。ラテン語 exsequi（最後まで追う）、ex + sequi（続く）。「やり遂げること」→ 刑を最後まで行う「死刑執行」。sequence と同じ。

en: The cardinal number occurring after forty-nine and before fifty-one.
A banknote or coin with a denomination of 50.
A batsman's score of at least 50 runs and less than 100 runs.

From Middle English fifty, from Old English fīftiġ, from Proto-Germanic *fimf tigiwiz (“five tens”). By surface analysis, five + -ty.

ex.en: The bank will cash your fifty dollar check.
ex.ja: 銀行に行けばその５０ドルの小切手を現金に換えてくれる。

ex.en: The man controlled the country for fifty years.
ex.ja: その男は５０年にわたってその国を支配した。

ex.en: Jack was tired from having walked fifty miles.
ex.ja: ジャックは５０マイル歩いてくたびれた。

note.ja: five + -ty。「5つの10」。

en: One who follows, comes after another.
Something that comes after another thing.

follower.ety: From Middle English folwer, folwere, folewer, from Old English folgere (“follower; attendant; disciple”), equivalent to follow + -er. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Foulger, West Frisian folger, Dutch volger, German Folger, Swedish följare.

ex.en: How many followers do you have on Twitter?
ex.ja: Twitterのフォロワーって何人ぐらいいるの？

ex.en: She is a follower of Freud.
ex.ja: 彼女はフロイトの信奉者だ。

ex.en: On the religious side, the decision caused serious dissension among followers.
ex.ja: 宗教的側面では、その決定は信者たちに深刻な分裂をもたらした。

note.ja: follow（従う）+ -er。「従う人」→ SNS の「フォロワー」。

en: A jester; a person whose role was to entertain a sovereign and the court (or lower personages).
A stock character typified by unintelligence, naïveté or lucklessness, usually as a form of comic relief; often used as a source of insig…
To trick; to deceive.
To act in an idiotic manner; to act foolishly.
Foolish.

fool.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *bʰelǵʰ-der.
Latin follis
Old French folbor.
Middle English fol
English fool
From Middle English fol (“fool”), from Old French fol (cf. modern French fou (“mad”)) from Latin follis. Doublet of fals and follis. Displaced native Old English dwæs.

ex.en: What a fool he is to leave school.
ex.ja: 学校を辞めるなんて彼はなんてばかだ。

ex.en: In a word, I think he's a fool.
ex.ja: 一言で言えば、彼は馬鹿だと思います。

ex.en: I don't like being made a fool of.
ex.ja: 人をばかにしないでもらいたい。

note.ja: ラテン語 follis（ふいご・空気袋）から。「中身が空っぽな人」→「ばか者」。folly と同じ。

en: A support structure comprising joined parts or conglomerated particles and intervening open spaces of similar or larger size.
The arrangement of support beams that represent a building's general shape and size.

ex.en: The framework of the new building is slowly taking form.
ex.ja: 新しい建物の骨組みが徐々に姿を見せてきている。

ex.en: The building will be made of concrete on a steel framework.
ex.ja: その建物は鋼鉄の骨組みにコンクリートで作られる事になっている。

note.ja: frame（枠）+ work（作り）。「骨組み・枠組み」。

en: The right to vote at a public election or referendum; see: suffrage.
A right or privilege officially granted to a person, a group of people, or a company by a government.
To confer certain powers on; grant a franchise to; authorize.
To give to others the rights to sell or distribute (goods or services).

franchise.ety: From Middle English franchise, fraunchise, from Old French franchise (“freedom”), a derivative of franc (“free”). More at frank.

ex.en: He owns a franchise of a famous coffee chain.
ex.ja: 彼は有名なコーヒーチェーンのフランチャイズ店を経営している。

note.ja: 古フランス語 franchise（自由）から。franc（自由な）。「（特別に与えられた）権利」→「営業権・選挙権」。frank と同じ。

en: Large movable item(s), usually in a room, which enhance(s) the room's characteristics, functionally or decoratively.
The harness, trappings etc. of a horse, hawk, or other animal.

furniture.ety: From Middle French fourniture (“a supply, or the act of furnishing”), from fournir (“to furnish”).

ex.en: There is too much furniture in the house.
ex.ja: その家には家具がたくさんありすぎる。

ex.en: There is too much furniture in this room.
ex.ja: この部屋には家具が多すぎる。

ex.en: We have just bought two pieces of furniture.
ex.ja: 私たちは家具を二つちょうど購入したところだ。

note.ja: フランス語 fourniture（備え付けるもの）から。fournir（備える）。furnish と同じ。

en: To include as a constituent part or functionality.
To join a group or an environment harmoniously; to make oneself fit in.

integrate.ety: First attested in the 1450's as an adjective, first attested in 1638 as a verb; from Middle English integrat(e) (“intact, whole”), borrowed from Latin integrātus, perfect passive participle of integrō (“to make whole, renew, repair, begin again”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from integer (“whole, fresh”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix). See integer and integral.

ex.en: This product is an intelligent integrated information system.
ex.ja: このプロダクトはインテリジェント総合情報システムです。

ex.en: Bear in mind that that school is an integrated junior high and high school.
ex.ja: その学校は、中・高一貫校だということを頭の片隅にでも入れておいて下さい。

ex.en: We are aiming for an integrated development zone that combines business and industrial quarters.
ex.ja: 工業区と商業区が一体となった総合的な開発区を目指しております。

note.ja: ラテン語 integrare（完全にする）から。integer（完全な）。「ひとつにまとめる」。integrity と同じ。

en: Of high or especially quick cognitive capacity, bright.
Well thought-out, well considered.
A member of the intelligentsia; an intelligent person.

From Middle French intelligent, from Latin intellegēns (“discerning”), present active participle of intellegō (“understand, comprehend”), itself from inter (“betwee

ex.en: What makes one person more intelligent than another?
ex.ja: ある人を別の人より賢くするのは何であるのか。

ex.en: Young as he is, he is quite intelligent.
ex.ja: 彼は若いけれどとても聡明です。

ex.en: He's intelligent, but I still don't like him.
ex.ja: 彼は頭がよいがやはり嫌いだ。

note.ja: intel（間で）+ lig（選ぶ）+ ent。物事の間から選び分けられる →「知能の高い・聡明な」。

en: The situation or occurrence in which two or more things act upon one another to produce an effect; the effect resulting from such a situa…
A conversation or exchange between people.

ex.en: Then interaction with others becomes important.
ex.ja: そこで他人との相互作用が大切になる。

ex.en: Tom has trouble with social interactions.
ex.ja: トムは社会的交流が苦手だ。

ex.en: It's the dynamic interaction between the characters that makes this novel so great.
ex.ja: 登場人物の躍動的な関わり合いこそがこの小説をかくも偉大なものとしている。

note.ja: inter（相互に）+ action（作用）。「相互作用・交流」。

en: A collimated stream, spurt or flow of liquid or gas from a pressurized container, an engine, etc.
A spout or nozzle for creating a jet of fluid.
To spray out of a container.
To spray with liquid from a container.
Propelled by turbine engines.

jet.ety:

Borrowed from French jet (“spurt”, literally “a throw”), from Old French get, giet, from Vulgar Latin *iectus, *jectus, from Latin iactus (“a throwing, a throw”), from iacere (“to throw”). See abject, ejaculate, gist, jess, jut. Cognate with Spanish echar.

ex.en: The jets took off one after another.
ex.ja: ジェット機が次々に離陸した。

ex.en: We saw a jet plane fly across the sky.
ex.ja: 私たちはジェット機が空を横切って飛ぶのを見た。

ex.en: Her son is a jet pilot.
ex.ja: 彼女の息子はジェット機のパイロットです。

note.ja: ラテン語 iactare（投げる）から。ject の仲間。勢いよく投げ出される →「噴出・ジェット（機）」。

en: A style of living that reflects the attitudes and values of a person or group.
The totality of the likes and dislikes of a particular section of the market, especially when expressed in terms of the products and serv…

lifestyle.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Germanic *lībanąder.
Proto-Germanic *lībą

English style
English lifestyle
From life + style.

ex.en: Take a fresh look at your lifestyle.
ex.ja: あなたのライフスタイルを見直してみましょう。

ex.en: One's lifestyle is largely determined by money.
ex.ja: 人の生活様式の大半はお金によって決まる。

ex.en: What is the definition of lifestyle disease?
ex.ja: 生活習慣病の定義は何ですか？

note.ja: life（生活）+ style（様式）。「生き方」。

en: A length of thread, line or rope that is doubled over to make an opening.
The opening so formed.
To form something into a loop.
To fasten or encircle something with a loop.

loop.ety: From Middle English loupe (“noose, loop”), earlier lowp-knot (“loop-knot”), of North Germanic origin, from Old Norse hlaup (“a run”), used in the sense of a "running knot", from hlaupa (“to leap”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *hlaupaną (“to leap, run”). Compare Swedish löp-knut (“loop-knot”), Danish løb-knude (“a running knot”), Danish løb (“a course”). More at leap. The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: Please keep us in the loop.
ex.ja: 私たちにも情報を共有していただければ助かります。

ex.en: This cold has knocked me for a loop.
ex.ja: 今度の風邪には本当にまいったよ。

ex.en: Jim was sewing loops on a flag this morning.
ex.ja: 今朝、ジムが旗に乳を付けていた。

note.ja: 中英語 loupe から。語源ははっきりしない。「輪」→ プログラムの「繰り返し」。

en: A pedestrianised street, especially a shopping precinct.
An enclosed shopping centre.
to beat with a mall, or mallet; to beat with something heavy; to bruise
to build up with the development of shopping malls

mall.ety: Probably from The Mall, a major street in London, England, which was originally a pall mall alley.

ex.en: I bought a new hat at the mall.
ex.ja: ショッピングモールで新しい帽子買ったんだ。

ex.en: Is there a bus that goes to the mall?
ex.ja: ショッピングモールへ行くためのバスはありますか。

ex.en: At the car wash next to the shopping mall.
ex.ja: ショッピングセンターの隣にある洗車場だよ。

note.ja: ロンドンの通り The Mall から。もとは pall-mall（木づちで球を打つ遊び）の競技場。並木道 →「ショッピングモール」。

en: Abroad, especially across the sea.
Used with ethnicities, nationalities, or religious affiliations: living (being resident) in a foreign country.
Abroad.
Across a sea; to an area across a sea.

overseas.ety: From earlier oversea, equivalent to oversea + -s. Compare West Frisian oerseesk, Dutch overzees, German Übersee, Danish oversøisk.

ex.en: I am working in the Overseas Operations Division.
ex.ja: 私は海外事業部で働いています。

ex.en: My father plans to go overseas next week.
ex.ja: 父は来週海外へ行く予定だ。

ex.en: I haven't heard from my son who's overseas.
ex.ja: 外国にいる息子から便りがない。

note.ja: over（越えて）+ seas（海）。「海を越えて」→「海外の」。

en: A substance used to polish.
Cleanliness; smoothness, shininess.
To shine; to make a surface very smooth or shiny by rubbing, cleaning, or grinding.
To refine; remove imperfections from.

polish.ety: From Middle English polishen, from Old French poliss-, stem of some of the conjugated forms of polir, from Latin polīre (“to polish, make smooth”), from Proto-Indo-European *pelh₂- (“to drive, strike, thrust”), from the notion of fulling cloth.

ex.en: When did the Japanese start eating polished rice?
ex.ja: いつから日本人は精白米を食べるようになったのですか？

ex.en: I got him to polish my shoes.
ex.ja: 私は彼に靴を磨いてもらった。

ex.en: The diamond in this ring is polished.
ex.ja: この指輪のダイヤは研磨してある。

note.ja: ラテン語 polire（磨く）から。「磨く」→「洗練」。Polish（ポーランドの）は Poland からで別語。

en: An act of recommending.
That which is recommended.

recommendation.ety: From Middle English recommendacioun, from Anglo-Norman recomendacion, from Medieval Latin recommendatio. By surface analysis, recommend + -ation.

ex.en: I've added my recommendations to improve the situation.
ex.ja: 状況を改善するための提案を付け加えておきました。

ex.en: My teacher wrote a recommendation for me.
ex.ja: 先生は私のために推薦状を書いた。

ex.en: The recommendation from my boss made all the difference.
ex.ja: 課長からもらった推薦状が物を言った。

note.ja: recommend（推薦する）+ -ation。re（強意）+ commend（ゆだねる）、com + mandare（任せる）。command と同じ。

en: To get back, to regain (a physical thing; in astronomy and navigation, sight of a thing or a signal).
To salvage, to extricate, to rescue (a thing or person).
A position of holding a firearm during exercises, whereby the lock is at shoulder height and the sling facing out.

recover.ety:
From Middle English recoveren, rekeveren, from Anglo-Norman recoverer and Old French recovrer, from Latin recuperāre, alternative form of reciperāre. Doublet of recuperate.
The noun is from Middle English recover, from the verb.

ex.en: The patient will soon recover from his illness.
ex.ja: 患者はまもなく病気が治るだろう。

ex.en: We'll find more engineers to recover the schedule.
ex.ja: スケジュールの遅れを取り戻すため、さらにエンジニアを手配します。

ex.en: To my relief, he recovered from his illness.
ex.ja: 私がほっとしたことに、彼は病気から回復した。

note.ja: ラテン語 recuperare（取り戻す）から古フランス語を経た語。「取り戻す」→「回復する」。cover とは別語源。

en: To make something loose.
To become loose.

relax.ety: From Middle English relaxen, from Old French relaxer, from Latin relaxāre (“relax, loosen, open”), from re- (“back”) + laxāre (“loosen”), from laxus (“loose, free”). By surface analysis, re- + lax (“open, free, loose”).

ex.en: He feels relaxed when he's playing the guitar.
ex.ja: 彼はギターを弾いているとリラックスできる。

ex.en: Let's stop working and relax for a while.
ex.ja: 仕事をやめてしばらく休みましょう。

ex.en: I can't relax when I'm talking with him.
ex.ja: 私は彼と話をしているとくつろぐ事ができない。

note.ja: ラテン語 relaxare ＝ re（元へ）+ laxare（緩める）。「緩める」→「くつろぐ」。lax（緩い）と同じ。

en: Suitable or fit to be relied on; worthy of dependence, reliance or trust; dependable, trustworthy
Such that either a sent packet will reach its destination, even if it requires retransmission, or the sender will be told that it didn't.
Something or someone reliable or dependable

reliable.ety:

From rely + -able.

ex.en: As far as I know, he is reliable.
ex.ja: 私の知る限りでは、彼は信頼できる。

ex.en: I got the news from a reliable source.
ex.ja: 私はそのニュースを確かな筋から得た。

ex.en: Japanese cars are for the most part reliable.
ex.ja: 大部分の日本車は信頼できる。

note.ja: rely（頼る）+ -able。「頼りになる」。

en: To trust; to have confidence in.
To depend; to be dependent upon.

rely.ety: From Middle English relien, from Old French relier (“fasten, attach, rally, oblige”), from Latin religo (“fasten, bind fast”), from re- + ligo.

ex.en: You must not rely upon such a man.
ex.ja: 君はそんな男を信頼してはならない。

ex.en: You must not rely too much on appearance.
ex.ja: 外見はあまり当てにしてはいけない。

ex.en: You can rely on their coming on time.
ex.ja: あの人達はきっと時間通りに来ますよ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 relier（結びつける）から。re + ligare（結ぶ）。「（〜に）結びつく」→「頼る」。religion、ally と同じ lig。

en: Worthy of remark; notable; interesting.
Uncommon; unusual.

ex.en: In recent years, science has made remarkable progress.
ex.ja: 近年科学は目覚しく進歩した。

ex.en: My sister has made remarkable progress in English.
ex.ja: 姉は注目すべき英語の進歩を遂げた。

ex.en: He has recently made remarkable progress in English.
ex.ja: 彼の英語は最近著しく進歩した。

note.ja: remark（気づく・述べる）+ -able。re + mark（印をつける）。「注目に値する」→「素晴らしい」。

en: Originally, the killing (and often burning) of a human being or an animal as an offering to a deity; later, also the offering of an objec…
A human being or an animal, or a physical object or immaterial thing (see etymology 1 sense 1.3), offered to a deity.
To offer (a human being or an animal, or an object) to a deity.
To destroy or kill (a human being or an animal); specifically (sciences), to kill (an animal) for a scientific experiment or test.
