ex.en: They made many sacrifices to get their own house.
ex.ja: 彼らは自分の家を持つために多くの犠牲を払った。

ex.en: I have made great sacrifices to come this far.
ex.ja: 多大な犠牲を払って、ここまで来た。

ex.en: She naturally sacrificed everything for the sake of raising her children.
ex.ja: 子どもたちを育てるために彼女は自らのすべてを犠牲にした。

note.ja: sacr（聖なる）+ i + fic（する）+ e。聖なるものにする →（神にささげる）→「犠牲（にする）」。

en: Only.
Unmarried (especially of a woman); widowed.
The bottom or plantar surface of the foot.
The bottom of a shoe or boot.
To put a sole on a shoe or a boot.

sole.ety: From Middle English sole, soule, from Old French sol, soul (“alone”), from Latin sōlus (“alone, single, solitary, lonely”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *swé (reflexive pronoun). Perhaps related to Old Latin sollus (“whole, complete”), from Proto-Indo-European *solh₂- (“safe, healthy”). More at save.

ex.en: Serving people is his sole purpose in life.
ex.ja: 人々に奉仕することが、彼の人生の唯一の目的だ。

ex.en: To serve people is his sole object in life.
ex.ja: 人々に奉仕することが、彼の人生の唯一の目的だ。

ex.en: Please bring shoes with a thick sole.
ex.ja: 持参する靴は、かかとのあるモノにしてください。

note.ja: ラテン語 solus（ひとりの）から。→「唯一の・単独の」。solo（独奏）、solitary（孤独な）も同じ。※「足の裏」の sole は別語。

en: To follow something in sequence or time.
To replace or supplant someone in order vis-à-vis an office, position, or title.

succeed.ety:
From Old French succeder, from Latin succedere (“to go under, go from under, come under, approach, follow, take the place of, receive by succession, prosper, be successful”).
Partly displaced English speed, of which the original sense “to succeed” only survives in a few fossilized expressions such as Godspeed.

ex.en: You are sure to succeed, whatever you do.
ex.ja: 何をしようとも、君は必ず成功する。

ex.en: If you try very hard, you will succeed.
ex.ja: 一生懸命努力すれば、あなたは成功するだろう。

ex.en: Had he worked harder, he could have succeeded.
ex.ja: もしもっと頑張っていれば、彼は成功できただろうに。

note.ja: suc（下から・次に）+ ceed（進む）。次に進む →「後を継ぐ・成功する」。

en: A rehearsal of what has occurred; narrative; discourse; statement; history; story.
A number told or counted off; a reckoning by count; an enumeration.

tale.ety:
From Middle English tale, from Old English talu (“tale, series, calculation”), from Proto-West Germanic *talu, from Proto-Germanic *talō (“calculation, number”), from Proto-Indo-European *del- (“to reckon, count”).
Cognate with West Frisian taal (“speech, language”), Dutch taal (“language, speech”), German Zahl (“number, figure”), Danish tale (“speech”), Icelandic tala (“speech, talk, discourse, number, figure”), Latin dolus (“guile, deceit, fraud”), Ancient Greek δόλος (dólos, “wile, bait”), Albanian ndjell (“to lure”), Northern Kurdish til (“finger”), Old Armenian տող (toł, “row”). Related t

ex.en: His book begins with a tale of country life.
ex.ja: 彼の本は田園生活の話から始まる。

ex.en: Don't tell tales out of school.
ex.ja: 学校の中の話を外でするな。

ex.en: The tale is familiar to us.
ex.ja: その物語はおなじみである。

note.ja: 古英語 talu（話・数えること）から。tell と同じ語根。teller（銀行の窓口係：お金を数える人）。

en: The short ton of 2000 pounds (about 907 kg), 20 hundredweights of 100 pounds avoirdupois each.
The long ton of 2240 pounds (about 1016 kg), 20 hundredweights of 112 pounds avoirdupois each.

ton.ety: Variant of tun (“cask”), influenced by Old French tonne (“ton”).

ex.en: This car can carry a load of 4 tons.
ex.ja: この車は４トン車だ。

ex.en: He plans to sell ten tons of tea.
ex.ja: 彼は茶の販売予定は十トンです。

ex.en: Steel production is estimated to reach 100 million tons this year.
ex.ja: 今年の鉄鋼生産は１億トンに達するものと見積もられている。

note.ja: tun（大きなたる）の変化形。大だる1つ分の重さ →「トン」。

en: One who enters into, or offers themselves for, any service of their own free will, especially when done without pay.
One who enters into military service voluntarily (but who, when in service, is subject to discipline and regulations like other soldiers)…
To enlist oneself as a volunteer.
To do or offer to do something voluntarily.

volunteer.ety: Borrowed from Middle French voluntaire, from Latin voluntārius (“willing, voluntary”); or from voluntary + -eer.

ex.en: The babies are taken care of by volunteers.
ex.ja: その赤ちゃんはボランティアによって世話される。

ex.en: I'd like to volunteer to go with Tom.
ex.ja: トムと一緒にボランティアに行きたいんです。

ex.en: There are people who engage in volunteer work.
ex.ja: ボランティアの仕事に従事する者もいる。

note.ja: フランス語 volontaire（自発的な）から。ラテン語 voluntas（意志）。「志願者」。voluntary と同じ。

en: The devotion accorded to a deity or to a sacred object.
The adoration (or latria) owed to God alone, as greater than the hyperdulia that is given to Saint Mary only and the veneration (or dulia…
To reverence (a deity, etc.) with supreme respect and veneration; to perform religious exercises in honour of.
To honour with extravagant love and extreme submission, as a lover; to adore; to idolize.

worship.ety: Inherited from Middle English worschipe /worthschipe, inherited from Old English weorþsċiepe. Cognate with Scots worschip (“worship”). By surface analysis, wor(th) + -ship.

ex.en: It is money that many people worship most.
ex.ja: 多くの人が最も崇拝するものはお金である。

ex.en: He regarded her with worship in his eyes.
ex.ja: 彼は崇拝の眼で彼女を眺めた。

ex.en: He worships money to exclusion of everything else.
ex.ja: 彼は他のものが目に入らないほどお金を崇拝している。

note.ja: 古英語 weorthscipe ＝ worth（価値）+ -ship。「価値を認めること」→「崇拝」。

en: Having worth, merit, or value.
Admirable or honourable.
A distinguished or eminent person.
a good, wise and virtuous person.
To render or treat as worthy.

worthy.ety: From Middle English worthy, wurthi, from Old English *weorþiġ (“worthy”), equivalent to worth + -y. Cognate with Dutch waardig (“worthy”), Middle Low German werdig (“worthy”), German würdig (“worthy”), Swedish värdig (“worthy”), Icelandic verðugur (“worthy”).

ex.en: Mary was not worthy of your trust.
ex.ja: メアリーはあなたの信頼を受けるに値しなかった。

ex.en: The offer is worthy of being considered.
ex.ja: その申し出は考慮に値する。

ex.en: This is a matter worthy of note.
ex.ja: これは注目に値することです。

note.ja: worth（価値）+ -y。「値する・立派な」。

en: A summons to arms, as on the approach of an enemy.
Any sound or information intended to give notice of approaching danger; a warning sound to arouse attention; a warning of danger.
To call to arms for defense.
To give (someone) notice of approaching danger or necessary action; to rouse to vigilance; to put on the alert.

alarm.ety: From Middle English alarme, alarom, borrowed from Middle French alarme, itself from Old Italian all'arme! (“to arms!, to the weapons!”), ultimately from Latin arma (“arms, weapons”).

ex.en: The news of the accident caused public alarm.
ex.ja: その事故のニュースで人々は不安になった。

ex.en: My alarm clock didn't go off this morning.
ex.ja: 私の目覚まし時計は今朝鳴らなかった。

ex.en: He set the alarm before going to bed.
ex.ja: 彼は寝る前に目覚ましをかけた。

note.ja: イタリア語 all'arme（武器を取れ）から。「警報」→「目覚まし時計」→「不安」。arms と同じ。

en: Of sound, a voice or an instrument, low in pitch or frequency.
A low spectrum of sound tones.
A section of a musical group that produces low-pitched sound, lower than the baritone and tenor.
To sound in a deep tone.

en: Covered in blood.
Characterised by bloodshed.
To stain with blood.
To draw blood from (one's opponent) in a fight.

bloody.ety: From Middle English blody, blodi, from Old English blōdiġ, blōdeġ (“bloody”), from Proto-West Germanic *blōdag, from Proto-Germanic *blōþagaz (“bloody”), equivalent to blood + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian bläidich, blöidig, blouderch (“bloody”), West Frisian bloedich (“bloody”), Dutch bloedig (“bloody”), German Low German blödig (“bloody”), German blutig (“bloody”), Danish blodig (“bloody”), Swedish blodig (“bloody”), Faroese blóðigur (“bloody”), Icelandic blóðugur (“bloody”). ex.en: What the bloody fuck is that?
ex.ja: 何だこりゃ？

ex.en: I'd like a Bloody Mary.
ex.ja: ブラッディーマリーをください。

ex.en: The walls are bloody.
ex.ja: 壁には血がついている。

note.ja: blood（血）+ -y。「血まみれの」→（英口語）強調の「ひどい」。

en: To draw air into (inhale), and expel air from (exhale), the lungs in order to extract oxygen and excrete waste gases.
To take in needed gases and expel waste gases in a similar way.

breathe.ety: From Middle English brethen (“to breathe, blow, exhale, odour”), derived from Middle English breth (“breath”). Eclipsed Middle English ethien and orðiæn, from Old English ēþian and orþian (“to breathe”); as well as Middle English anden, onden, from Old Norse anda (“to breathe”). More at breath.

ex.ja: ただ呼吸しているだけでは生きていることにならない。

ex.ja: おくびにも出すな。

ex.en: We breathe, eat, and speak with our mouth.
ex.ja: 私たちは口で息をし、食べ、話します。

note.ja: breath（息）の動詞形。「呼吸する」。

en: The buttocks or anus (used as a minced oath in idiomatic expressions; less objectionable than arse/ass).
The whole buttocks and pelvic region that includes one's private parts.
To join at the butt, end, or outward extremity; to terminate; to be bounded; to abut.

A distinguishing feature of a person or thing, a part of mental or physical behavior.
The integer part of a logarithm.

ex.ja: ある種の行動はその少年に特徴的だ。

note.ja: character（性格・特徴）+ -istic。ギリシャ語 kharaktēr（刻印）。「特徴的な」。

en: The act of collaborating.
A production or creation made by collaborating.

collaboration.ety: Originated 1855–60 from French collaboration, from Late Latin collaboratus + -ion, from Latin con- (“with”) + labōrō (“work”). Morphologically collaborate + -ion.

ex.en: Collaboration has apparently paid off for both of them.
ex.ja: 両者にとって協力が実を結んだようだ。

note.ja: col（共に）+ labor（働く）+ ation。共に働くこと →「協力・共同制作」。

To trick, lie or defraud, usually for personal gain.

ex.en: Every programming language has its pros and cons.
ex.ja: どのプログラミング言語も一長一短だ。

ex.en: There are pros and cons to anything.
ex.ja: なんにでも、長所と短所の両方がある。

ex.en: There were a lot of opinions, pro and con, on this question.
ex.ja: この問題に対して可否の論が色々とあった。

note.ja: 「だます」は confidence trick（信用させる詐欺）の短縮。「反対論」はラテン語 contra（反対に）の短縮で、pros and cons（賛否）。

en: The thought process of considering, of taking multiple or specified factors into account (with of being the main corresponding adposition).
Something considered as a reason or ground for a (possible) decision.

consideration.ety: From Middle English consideracioun, from Old French consideracion, from Latin cōnsīderātiō. By surface analysis, consider + -ation.

ex.en: We should have taken the schedule into consideration.
ex.ja: 私たちは日程を考慮に入れるべきだった。

ex.en: Taking everything into consideration, he bought the car.
ex.ja: すべてのことを考慮して彼はその車を買った。

ex.en: We have to take this problem into consideration.
ex.ja: 私たちはこの問題を考慮に入れなくてはならない。

note.ja: consider（考慮する）+ -ation。「考慮・思いやり」。consider はラテン語 considerare（星をよく見る）とされる。

en: Essential or decisive for determining the outcome or future of something; extremely important; vital.

crucial.ety:
1706, from French crucial, a medical term for ligaments of the knee (which cross each other), from Latin crux, crucis (“cross”) (English crux), from the Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to turn, to bend”).
The meaning “decisive, critical” is extended from a logical term, Instantias Crucis, adopted by Francis Bacon in his influential Novum Organum (1620); the notion is of cross fingerboard signposts at forking roads, thus a requirement to choose.

ex.en: Why isn't Tom here at this crucial moment?
ex.ja: なんでこの肝心な時にトムがいないんだよ！

ex.en: We are facing a crucial time.
ex.ja: 今が我々にとって一番大切な時だ。

ex.en: It is crucial for world peace.
ex.ja: それは、世界の平和のためにとても大切なことです。

note.ja: ラテン語 crux（十字架・分かれ道）から。「十字路の・分かれ目となる」→「決定的な」。cross と同系。

en: Relying upon; depending upon.
Having a probability that is affected by the outcome of a separate event.
A person who relies on another for support or sustenance, particularly financial support.
An element in phrase or clause structure that is not the head. Includes complements, modifiers and determiners.

dependent.ety: From Middle English dependaunt, dependent, from Middle French dependant (present participle of dependre (“to depend”)) and Latin dēpendēns (present participle of dēpendeō (“to depend”)). By surface analysis, depend + -ent.

ex.en: The boy is totally dependent on his parents.
ex.ja: その男の子は両親に完全に頼っている。

ex.en: The industry is heavily dependent on government funding.
ex.ja: その産業は政府の資金援助に大きく依存している。

ex.en: Though 38, he is still dependent on his parents.
ex.ja: 彼は３８歳なのに両親に頼りきりです。

note.ja: de（下に）+ pend（ぶら下がる）+ ent。下にぶら下がっている →「頼っている・依存した」。

en: Characterized by having two (usually equivalent) components.
Pertaining to two, pertaining to a pair of.
Of an item that is one of a pair, the other item in the pair.
Of a regular polyhedron with V vertices and F faces, the regular polyhedron having F vertices and V faces.
To convert from single to dual; specifically, to convert a single-carriageway road to a dual carriageway.

dual.ety:

ex.ja: アーノルドは二重人格の事例を扱っている。

ex.en: He has a dual personality.
ex.ja: 彼は二重人格者だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 dualis（2の）から。duo（2）。「二重の」。double と同系。duel（決闘）とは別語。

ex.en: My car is equipped with a CD player.
ex.ja: 私の車はＣＤプレーヤーを装備している。

ex.en: Her kitchen is equipped with labor-saving devices.
ex.ja: 彼女の台所は手間を省ける装置が装備されている。

ex.en: The soldiers were equipped with weapons.
ex.ja: その兵士たちは武装していた。

note.ja: equip（装備する）+ -ed。「備えた」。equipment と同じ。

en: Pertaining to or founded on experiment.
Serving to be experimented upon; used in an experiment.
The subject of an experiment.

ex.en: Our experimental results left something to be desired.
ex.ja: 実験の結果は今ひとつぱっとしなかった。

ex.en: There must be a defect in the experimental method.
ex.ja: 実験方法に欠陥があるに違いない。

ex.en: Something is wrong with the experimental apparatus.
ex.ja: 実験用器具が故障している。

note.ja: experiment（実験）+ -al。「実験的な」。

en: A device which separates a suspended, dissolved, or particulate matter from a fluid, solution, or other substance; any device that separa…
Electronics or software that separates unwanted signals (for example noise) from wanted signals or that attenuates selected frequencies.
To sort, sift, or isolate.
To diffuse; to cause to be less concentrated or focused.

filter.ety: From Middle English filtre, from Medieval Latin filtrum (compare also Old French feutre (“felt; filter”)), from Frankish *filtir, from Proto-West Germanic *felt. See felt. Doublet of phin.

ex.en: Somebody bought me a new water filter.
ex.ja: 新しい整水器、買ってもらったんだ。

ex.en: I was bought a new water filter.
ex.ja: 新しい整水器、買ってもらったんだ。

ex.en: This store uses a water filter.
ex.ja: 当店の水は浄水器を使用しています。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 filtrum（フェルト）から。フェルトでこして液体をろ過したことから。felt と同じ語源。

en: Any of the collections of many millions or billions of stars, galactic dust, black holes, etc. existing as independent and coherent syste…
An assemblage of things or people seen as luminous or brilliant.
To furnish with galaxies.

galaxy.ety: From Middle English galaxye, galaxie, from Old French galaxie, from Latin galaxias, from Ancient Greek γαλαξίας (galaxías, “Milky Way”), shortening of γαλαξίας κύκλος (galaxías kúklos, “milky circle”), from γάλα (gála, “milk”).

ex.en: There are many galaxies in the universe.
ex.ja: 宇宙にはたくさんの銀河がある。

ex.en: We live in a galaxy.
ex.ja: 私たちは銀河に住んでいます。

ex.en: There are innumerable stars in the galaxy.
ex.ja: 銀河系には無数の星がある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 galaxias（乳の）から。gala（乳）。天の川（Milky Way）を「乳の道」と呼んだことから。

en: The eyeball.
A spherical model of Earth or of another planet.
To become spherical.
To make spherical.

globe.ety: From late Middle English globe, from Middle French globe, from Old French globe, borrowed from Latin globus. Doublet of globus.

ex.en: I travel to all parts of the globe.
ex.ja: 私は世界中を旅行する。

ex.en: The earth is not a perfect globe.
ex.ja: 地球は完全な球体ではない。

ex.en: She has traveled all over the globe.
ex.ja: 彼女は地球のあちこちを旅行した。

note.ja: ラテン語 globus（球）から。「球体」→「地球・地球儀」。global と同じ。

en: A hollow place in the earth; an abyss; a deep chasm or basin.
That which swallows irretrievably; a whirlpool; a sucking eddy.
To engulf.
To award a degree to somebody who has only just passed sufficiently.

gulf.ety: From Middle English gulf, goulf, golf, from Old French golf, from Italian golfo, from Late Latin colfos, from Ancient Greek κόλπος (kólpos, “bosom, gulf”), of obscure origin, but possibly from Proto-Indo-European *kʷelp- (“to curve, arch”).

ex.en: How do you feel about the Gulf War?
ex.ja: 湾岸戦争についてどう思いますか。

ex.en: What do you think about the Gulf War?
ex.ja: 湾岸戦争についてどう思いますか。

ex.en: The ship is bound for the Gulf of Mexico.
ex.ja: その船はメキシコ湾行きである。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kolpos（ふところ・湾）からイタリア語 golfo を経た語。「湾」→「隔たり」。

An especially significant or interesting detail or event or period of time.
To make prominent; emphasize.
To be a highlight of.

ex.en: Every statement highlights their own imperfections.
ex.ja: 発言するたびにボロが出る。

en: Something that is intended.
The state of someone’s mind at the time of committing an offence.
Firmly fixed or concentrated on something.
Engrossed.

intent.ety: Existing since Middle English entente, from Old French entent or entente, ultimately from Latin intentus. Modified later in spelling to align more closely with the Latin word. Compare intention.

ex.en: My eyes were intent on the scene.
ex.ja: 私の目はその光景に吸い付けられた。

ex.ja: 彼はフランス語を懸命に勉強してきた。

ex.ja: ファッション研究にニューヨークに行くのだと彼女は堅く心にきめている。

en: The act of judging.
The power or faculty of performing such operations; especially, when unqualified, the faculty of judging or deciding rightly, justly, or …

judgment.ety: From Middle English juggement, borrowed from Old French jugement, from Late Latin iūdicāmentum, from Latin iūdicō. Partially displaced doom. By surface analysis, judge + -ment.

ex.en: I've always trusted your judgment.
ex.ja: 君の判断をいつも信じていました。

note.ja: judge（判断する）+ -ment。ラテン語 judicare ＝ jus（法）+ dicere（言う）。「法を言い渡す」。judgement とも書く。

en: A young servant or follower; a trained military attendant in service of a lord.
A minor nobleman with an honourable military rank who had served as a page and squire.
To confer knighthood upon.
To promote (a pawn) to a knight.

knight.ety: From Middle English knight, knyght, kniht, from Old English cniht (“boy; servant, knight”), from Proto-West Germanic *kneht.

ex.en: Look at that knight on the horse.
ex.ja: 馬上の騎士をみてごらん。

ex.en: The knight is not so much brave as reckless.
ex.ja: その騎士は勇敢と言うよりも向こう見ずだ。

ex.en: I tilt my head. Not the pawn, but the knight?
ex.ja: 僕は首をひねる。このポーンではなくて、こっちのナイトを・・・。

note.ja: 古英語 cniht（若者・従者）から。ドイツ語 Knecht（下僕）と同じ。「従者」→「騎士」。k は発音しない。

en: A visual symbol or emblem that acts as a trademark or a means of identification of a company or organization.
An audio recording for the same purpose; a jingle.

ex.en: Have you ever seen this logo before?
ex.ja: このロゴ見たことある？

ex.en: I like the Tatoeba logo.
ex.ja: 私はタトエバのロゴが好きだ。

ex.ja: AロゴはA株式会社の商標または登録 商標です。

note.ja: logotype の短縮。ギリシャ語 logos（言葉）+ typos（型）。

en: Fully developed; grown up in terms of physical appearance, behaviour or thinking; ripe.
Brought to a state of complete readiness.
To proceed toward maturity: full development or completion (either of concrete or of abstract things, e.g. plans, judgments, qualities).
To attain maturity, to become mature or ripe.

mature.ety: From late Middle English mature, from Middle French mature, from Latin mātūrus. Doublet of maduro. Partially displaced ripe, from Old English rīpe (“ripe, mature”).

ex.en: I wanted to meet a really mature woman.
ex.ja: 私は真の大人の女性に会いたいと思った。

ex.en: She had matured into an excellent woman.
ex.ja: 彼女は素敵な女性に成熟していた。

ex.en: Jane is mature beyond her years.
ex.ja: ジェーンは年齢以上に大人びている。

note.ja: ラテン語 maturus（熟した・時宜を得た）から。「成熟した」。premature と同じ。

en: Not at war; not disturbed by strife or turmoil.
Inclined to peace.
A non-player character who is not hostile to the player.

peaceful.ety: From Middle English peesful, pesful, paisful, pesefull. By surface analysis, peace + -ful. Displaced native Old English friþsum.

ex.en: Never have I seen such a peaceful scene.
ex.ja: こんなのどかな眺めは見たことがない。

ex.en: Never have I seen such a peaceful sight.
ex.ja: 私は今までに、これほどのどかな光景を見たことがない。

ex.en: My father died a peaceful death last night.
ex.ja: 父は昨晩安らかに死んだ。

note.ja: peace（平和）+ -ful。peace はラテン語 pax。「平和な」。
